articles.title: Logitech Pebble Mouse 2 review: the perfect travel mouse but not a fit for gaming or productivity
articles.content: The Logitech Pebble Mouse 2’s is a mouse that's primary purpose is to be portable. It’s the perfect device to take on the go with you but this does come at a slight detriment in the form of its ergonomics and any other flashy features. It’s slimline at just over 0.98 inches / 25mm tall when sat on your desk but is relatively flat when it comes to overall shape. There’s a small incline, making it slightly taller towards the back end that sits in your palm, but this is in no way comparable to a normal curved mouse shape, which sits snugly and comfortably in your hand, particularly if you opt for a claw grip. (Image credit: Future) When holding and using the device, the shape is something you have to get used to with time but I barely noticed the difference after a while. Its diminutive size is something that's likely only suited to smaller hands, as it can become uncomfortable using the device for long periods of time for those with larger ones. However, in turn, the size of the mouse is absolutely perfect for those who need a reliable mouse on the go — it's so small it can fit in your pocket without any issue. You can pick up the Logitech Pebble Mouse 2 in Pink, Black or White. There are also currently two limited designs on offer: the Study Buddy and the Coffee Cat, both created by designer EdgyKatrina. While already adorable in form factor, these limited edition designs take the mouse to the next level in terms of style — as a cat person, the Coffee Cat edition really tugged on my heart strings. You don’t get any extra buttons on this mouse, featuring just the right click, left click and the scroll wheel, which can also be pressed as a third button. You can reprogram the middle click using the Logi Options+ app that's available on both Windows and Mac. (Image credit: Future) Contributing to the portability is the silent touch technology, which makes both buttons and the scroll wheel significantly quieter than a normal mouse button. This makes it great to use when you’re commuting or in a situation where you don’t want to disturb those around you. Another benefit is that they feel satisfying to press — not in a mechanical clicky way but more of a haptic touch style. The mouse is powered by a single AA battery that can be replaced by removing the faceplate of the mouse, which is attached via magnets and can simply be pulled off and placed back on. Logitech claims that the mouse can provide up to 24 months of battery life based on computing conditions — something that's pretty much impossible for me to verify right now. I’ll get back to you in a couple of years and confirm. When it comes to connectivity, the mouse offers Bluetooth as an option but it can be connected to three devices at once and switched between all three using a button on the base. I found this particularly useful when I was traveling with both my laptop and iPad, as it allowed me to pretty seamlessly control both with one device. It does work with the Logi Bolt USB receiver, but this needs to be bought separately. Future Future The feet of the mouse don’t offer as smooth of a glide as my usual mouse — the Razer Cobra Pro — or even any of the other gaming mice I have tested. It’s not something that is off-putting in any way but is still worth noting considering it definitely feels like it has the smallest bit of resistance when using it. Outside of this, using the mouse felt pretty flawless for its seemingly intended purpose: being used on the go. I was able to stuff it in my bag, grab it when needed and put it to use across a range of devices whenever I needed. Despite being small, it felt comfortable to use once I got used to the shape and size. (Image credit: Future) It’s fantastic to not have to worry about the battery. The Logitech Pebble 2 can sit for — at least what feels like — an eternity at the bottom of my backpack, ready for whenever I next need it without me having to charge it between work days or trips. While I enjoy using the mouse and will…

articles.title: Lenovo leak reveals floating touchscreen that could debut at CES 2027
articles.content: A new leak describes Lenovo’s ‘aerial display’ tech The 12-inch floating screen could arrive at CES 2027 Prices, exact sizes and other specs remain unknown for now CES 2027 is still a few months away, but that hasn’t stopped one of its most intriguing products from leaking out ahead of schedule. As detailed on the Dutch website NieuweMobiel , Lenovo is apparently working on a floating “aerial display” named Project Hoverview that could bring with it a major wow factor. Unlike a 3D hologram , NieuweMobiel says Lenovo plans to incorporate a 2D image into Project Hoverview. It will apparently come with a 9:5 aspect ratio and feature touch-enabled capabilities. Exact dimensions aren’t known, but NieuweMobiel has estimated that the display could measure around 12 inches (although the outlet concedes that it could fall anywhere between 10 and 15 inches). The display will likely be built into a large countertop. However, before you start dreaming about installing one of these in your home, NieuweMobiel cautions that the device appears to be intended for retail settings (for now, at least). It isn't a compact screen that can be used as a television or second display for a computer, for example, but is rather intended to be fixed in place inside its bulky table-like housing. NieuweMobiel suggests two ways that Project Hoverview could be used. The first is as a public demonstration tool, where users could interact with the screen — including with touch gestures — without physically touching the device, which would cut down on the smudges that typically bedevil physical demo screens. The other use case is for fairs and trade events, where companies could show off new products and features to interested customers. Neither of these use cases suggest the device will be intended for the home, and the fact that it is apparently built into a countertop means it doesn’t appear to be well suited for comfortably watching TV in a relaxed environment. Pros and cons NieuweMobiel NieuweMobiel Other than the images provided by NieuweMobiel, very little appears to be known about Lenovo’s Project Hoverview. It’s not clear how Lenovo will make the display float or how it will enable users to interact with it using touch gestures. Presumably, these details will be revealed at CES 2027. We can perhaps glean some hints from other floating displays, as Project Hoverview is not the first attempt at this technology. Other examples use a plate of microscopic mirrors to bend light from a physical display at project its content into the air. Sensors track your finger movements to enable the touch functionality. There are drawbacks to this kind of tech. Viewing angles are limited, bright lights can interfere with the picture, and the lack of physical feedback when using gesture controls can be unsatisfying. We’ll have to see if Lenovo is able to address any of those concerns at CES 2027. If it can, Project Hoverview could make for an interesting advancement of the technology — just not in your home, for now.
articles.author: Alex Blake
articles.fingerprint: 2027 ces could debut floating leak lenovo reveals touchscreen

articles.title: Iowans Brace For Lead Dust Cloud As Army Plans to Detonate 5 Tons of Bomb-Making Chemicals
articles.content: The U.S. Army plans to detonate roughly five tons of unstable lead azide explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Friday. "The detonation will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground," an advisory states. "Lead is toxic to humans and animals. The goal of this advisory is to provide the public with actionable information out of an abundance of caution to minimize lead exposure." PBS reports: Officials have released maps showing the potential drift north, and the Army will continue to update the maps based on weather. Some schools in the region have already canceled classes. Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but thousands more could be affected. The vibrations from the two blasts will be quick but could break old windows in town. The resulting dust is expected to linger for no more than one hour, depending on wind speed, officials said. While the Army recommends cleaning cars, windowsills and outdoor surfaces, residents have taken to social media to voice concern and question whether that will be enough. [...] Middletown residents learned in March that the Army needed to dispose of several dozen barrels containing lead azide, after the ammunition plant paused operations as part of a review and the degraded material was discovered. "The safety of our people and our neighbors is non-negotiable," Lt. Col. Daniel Nosse, commander of the plant, said at the time, acknowledging the volatility of the chemical compound used in munitions production. The Army shared more details during a public meeting in Middletown in October, advising that a detonation was planned for an unspecified date in November. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Get an RTX 5070 for just $839.99, a rare savings in the GPU wasteland
articles.content: Buying a nice graphics card... in this economy? After Nvidia shipped all the GPUs to AI data centers? Yes, it's actually possible, if you act fast. Newegg is currently running a deal on a GeForce RTX 5070 12 GB , in this case the MSI Ventus 2X OC variant, and you can get a hold of one for $839.99 after you apply the coupon. That's $60 off the going rate of about $900 for even the most affordable variants of this class of card. Better act fast, before Jensen finds himself yet another person to share a plate of chips with. Get an MSI GeForce RTX 5070 Ventus 2X OC 12 GB for $839.99 at Newegg. In this price bracket of $839.99, the RTX 5070 is actually a heck of a good deal in this age of scarce, price-inflated cards. This card slots in just behind AMD's pricier RX 9070 in terms of raw performance, a gap that can be closed by Nvidia's superior DLSS upscaling quality and cleaner frame generation. The price is correspondingly lower too, as the red team's GPUs have steeply climbed in price lately. GeForce RTX 5070 Ventus 2X OC 12 GB: was $899.99 now $839.99 Our review found that it's capable of playing most games at 1440p with high frame rates, at high detail levels with ray tracing. It'll also manage smooth 4K gameplay with raytracing across many titles, with the help of DLSS and DLSS FG. View Deal Future Future Future As you can see from the handy chart above with our testing at 1080p, the standard RTX 5070 occupies pretty much the precise middle slot on the green team's lineup. If you flip through the album, you'll see we found that it's capable of playing most any game at 1440p and high framerates, at high detail levels with raytracing. It'll also manage 4K gameplay with raytracing across many titles, with the help of DLSS and DLSS FG, and with judicious tuning of the highest graphical settings that are usually diminishing returns anyway. Not only that, prices for faster options are so far out there that their value propositions compared to this RTX 5070 range from iffy to laughable. Radeon RX 9070 XTs start at a grand, while the cheapest of Nvidia's RTX 5080 cards go for well over $2,200, with most models sitting around $2,500. As for the RTX 5090s, those are all speed-learning Mandarin and Cantonese and unavailable for comment. For now, this deal on a GeForce RTX 5070 12 GB is one of the best we've seen for the first day of Black Friday, but you'll need to pounce fast.

articles.title: This versatile Weber Q barbecue can grill, roast and bake — and it's now 15% off at Amazon
articles.content: Summer is almost upon us in Australia, and if your outdoor cooking setup is in need of an upgrade, I've spotted a timely Black Friday deal on one of Weber's most versatile compact barbecues. Right now, you can pick up the Weber Q2200N Premium gas barbecue for AU$466.65 in the Amazon Black Friday sale , down from AU$549. That's a 15% saving of AU$82.35, although the offer only applies to the rather fetching Sky Blue colourway. It’s just one of a multitude of Weber Black Friday deals available at Amazon . View the latest Black Friday deals in Australia from a variety of retailers Q Premium Gas BBQ (Q2200N – 3rd Gen): was $549 now $466.65 Don't let its compact dimensions fool you. The Q2200N has a generous 2,064cm² cooking area, which Weber claims is large enough to accommodate up to 12 burgers at once. And thanks to its high-domed lid and integrated thermometer, it's capable of roasting and baking as well as grilling. View Deal The Q2200N is part of Weber's third-generation Q range, bringing a larger cooking area and a more convenient front-facing grease tray compared to its predecessor. Other welcome features include electronic ignition, porcelain-enamelled cast-iron cooking grills and removable side tables. What's particularly appealing is that the Q2200N offers the same cooking area as the more expensive Q2800N+ (which also gets a 15% discount for Black Friday), although it misses out on that model's second burner. This gives the Q2800N+ greater temperature flexibility, allowing it to reach higher searing temperatures while also maintaining lower heat for slow cooking. If you're mainly grilling burgers, steaks and sausages, however, the Q2200N should be more than capable. And if you'd prefer a more traditional freestanding barbecue setup, the Q2200N is also compatible with Weber's portable BBQ cart , which raises it to a more comfortable cooking height. It's sold separately, but the wheeled, foldable design makes it a handy addition for smaller outdoor spaces. If you're looking for a quality barbecue that won't dominate your balcony, courtyard or patio, the Weber Q2200N is a compelling option. And while 15% off isn't the biggest Black Friday discount I've seen, saving more than AU$80 on a premium Weber is certainly better than paying full price.

articles.title: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 launches in review, part 2
articles.content: Once a model is in production, the questions change. Teams want to know which configuration the model should run on now that traffic is real, how to fit more models onto GPUs they already pay for, what to do when the next model is too large for one machine, why requests wait in one Region while GPUs sit idle in another, and why latency rose when nobody changed anything. This post takes those questions in the order teams usually meet them. For HyperPod Inference, it listed additional routing strategies, broader support for model serving frameworks, and expanded multi-Region networking. The Inference Gateway delivers the routing, and managed NVIDIA Dynamo is a new serving framework. For managed endpoints, the roadmap pointed to deeper integration with the rest of the AWS AI landscape. Inference recommendations now run from Amazon SageMaker AI Studio, the SageMaker Python SDK, and the coding agents engineers already use, and endpoints can now route requests across Regions and accounts. To keep each section concrete, we follow one hypothetical team through the blog post. In the spring, they launched a customer support assistant on a 70B-parameter model behind a single SageMaker AI endpoint, using the launches from part 1. By the fall, they need to support more product lines, adopt a larger reasoning model, serve customers in a second Region, and keep their GPU bill flat. The launches at a glance Figure 1: The five stages in this post and the launches in each Choose the right configuration from wherever you work The team picked its first configuration from a benchmark run in April. Since then, they have added four LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adapters, one for each product line, and the product team has set a target of 500 milliseconds for time to first token (TTFT) at peak load. The April configuration was never tested against either change. The engineers who will re-run the analysis work in notebooks and coding agents, and few of them use the console. Inference recommendations launched in April as an API. Four updates since then make it available in more of the places teams work, and let it answer two harder questions: how many adapters an endpoint can carry, and how much concurrency it can take before it misses a latency target. A new agent skill brings the same expertise into coding agents. Inference recommendations in SageMaker AI Studio (July 2026) Blog: Launching UI for generative AI inference recommendations in Amazon SageMaker AI The April launch automated instance, container, and optimization selection through APIs. Inference recommendations are now also available in SageMaker AI Studio as a guided, low-code workflow. In Studio, choose Jobs , then Inference optimization . Choose a use-case profile (Interact, Generate, Summarize, or Custom), an optimization goal (minimize latency, maximize throughput, or minimize cost), and a model from SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), the Model Registry, or an existing SageMaker model. SageMaker AI benchmarks candidate configurations on real GPU infrastructure using NVIDIA AIPerf and applies techniques that match the goal, such as speculative decoding for throughput or kernel tuning for latency. You compare the ranked results by TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, and cost, and then deploy the chosen configuration to a real-time endpoint from Studio. Inference recommendations in the SageMaker Python SDK v3 (August 2026) Blog: LLM optimization integration for Amazon SageMaker Python SDK Benchmarking and recommendations previously required SageMaker AI Studio or direct Boto3 calls. They are now part of the SageMaker Python SDK v3 (version 3.17.0 and later), the same interface teams use for training and deployment, so the workflow fits into notebooks, CI pipelines, and MLOps workflows. You can benchmark a live endpoint against your workload traffic, generate ranked recommendations for a latency, throughput, or cost goal, and deploy the top-ranked…

articles.title: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock
articles.content: Kimi Code CLI is an open source coding agent from Moonshot AI, the creator of the Kimi series of open-weight foundation models. Previously, using Kimi Code with models on Amazon Bedrock meant configuring a generic connection “provider” with an Amazon Bedrock API key. For many AWS customers, this meant introducing an extra credential to obtain and protect. With v2.7.0, Moonshot AI adds a native bedrock provider to the CLI. You can now configure the agent to use your standard AWS credential chain, including named profiles and single sign-on (SSO), instead of creating and managing a separate API key. In this post, we show you how to connect Kimi Code CLI to models on Amazon Bedrock using your existing AWS credentials. We use Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed as an example, which supports streaming, configurable reasoning, image input, and client-side tool calling. What’s new Amazon Bedrock provides pay-per-token inference for a range of open and proprietary models from leading providers, available through standard APIs . Processing stays within the AWS data boundary, as detailed in the Data protection section of the User Guide. The model cards detail which APIs and features are supported for each model. In older versions of the Kimi Code CLI, you could connect to Amazon Bedrock through a provider with type = "openai" or type = "openai_responses" . These use the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions or Responses APIs, respectively. This approach required you to set the regional base_url and provide an Amazon Bedrock API key . The key could be short-term or long-term, but it was a separate credential for you to obtain and manage. The native provider changes that setup: Use your existing AWS authentication workflow. The bedrock provider can resolve temporary credentials through the standard AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) credential chain. You can use the default chain or select a named profile, including a profile backed by SSO. Override the protocol for each model, if needed. The provider infers an API format and regional endpoint from the model ID, but you can change them as detailed in the “Override endpoint URL and protocol” section of this post. AWS recommends short-term credentials over long-term credentials. This new path reduces reliance on manually managed API keys, but it doesn’t change your responsibility to protect AWS credentials and scope permissions appropriately. How it works The native provider handles authentication and request routing in four steps: Resolve AWS credentials. Unless you configure an Amazon Bedrock API key, the bedrock provider uses the standard AWS credential chain in your environment. You can set AWS_PROFILE to select a specific named profile . Generate a short-lived bearer token. The provider uses @aws/bedrock-token-generator to create a short-term Amazon Bedrock API key, and renews it when necessary. You don’t need to place any AWS access key or manually generated Amazon Bedrock key in the Kimi Code config.toml . However, an explicit key given through api_key or api_key_env takes precedence if you provide it. Build the regional endpoint. The provider resolves AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and constructs the appropriate bedrock-runtime endpoint for the model’s inferred API. For Kimi models, this resolves to the recommended OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions path. Call the selected inference profile. The model alias maps to an Amazon Bedrock model or inference profile ID. This example uses the global inference profile global.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1 . The global. prefix selects the profile, while AWS_REGION determines the regional endpoint that receives your request. The CLI then streams the model response and can use the model’s client-side tool-calling support during coding tasks. Authentication, authorization, model access, and network connectivity must all succeed for a request to complete. The ephemeral API keys generated by the provider are valid for up to 12 hours or your AWS session length,…

articles.title: The Large Hadron Collider is being taken apart to fit magnets that have never run in an accelerator before
articles.content: CERN is pulling the LHC's old NbTi focusing magnets to fit Nb3Sn quadrupoles as part of its High-Luminosity LHC-centric upgrade The replacements are the first Nb3Sn magnets ever run in a working accelerator The High-Luminosity LHC is scheduled to start up in June 2030, about a year later than originally planned The Large Hadron Collider has been switched off since late June 2026 , and CERN's engineers are now taking it apart. Since September 7, teams on either side of the ATLAS and CMS experiments have been dismantling the machine to remove 28 superconducting magnets , including the "inner triplets" that squeeze the proton beams just before they collide. Their replacements are made from niobium-tin (Nb3Sn), a superconductor that keeps working in far stronger magnetic fields than the niobium-titanium (NbTi) the LHC was built with, but, as a trade-off, it is too brittle to bend once it has formed. A manufacturing challenge meets evolving requirements as CERN looks to the future The manufacturing, however, is challenging, to say the least, given the brittle nature of the replacement material. Just how awkward that makes the entire process is the subject of a study published September 24 2026 in IEEE Transactions on Applied Superconductivity and written up by IEEE Spectrum on November 10. Across the program, 250 coils were produced, and 25 failed, either through human error or because the process left them with substandard electrical or mechanical properties. One was scrapped because a single metal particle trapped between the coil and a protective component was suspected of affecting its performance. That 90% yield aligns closely with the 89% the US side reported after its first 110 coils in 2024. The High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), now scheduled to start in June 2030 , is meant to raise the number of proton collisions in each bunch crossing from about 60 today to between 140 and 200. More collisions mean more chances to catch rare events, and a lot more data for a lab that passed an exabyte of storage capacity in 2023 and already runs more than 120,000 hard drives in its central data center. Getting there depends on focusing the beams harder at the collision points, which is the inner triplets' job. The new quadrupoles have a 150 mm aperture, up from 70 mm in the magnets being removed. The wider bore gives the beam room to swell as it passes through the triplet, which in turn lets the magnets focus it to a smaller spot where the protons meet. The choice of superconducting material comes with its own challenges, however: NbTi is ductile and can be extruded and drawn like copper wire. Nb3Sn is an intermetallic compound that forms only around 650 °C and is brittle and strain-sensitive once formed. Winding a finished superconductor is therefore off the table, so the coils are made by a process called wind-and-react. Nb3Sn itself is hardly new; It has been a staple of high-field research magnets for decades and is used in fusion projects such as ITER. What CERN says is new is accelerator-quality Nb3Sn at this length; its 7.2 m quadrupoles are the longest such magnets ever built. Although the current process is only just getting underway, the stakes extend well past 2030. In May, the CERN Council named the electron-positron Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee) its preferred next flagship, with a decision on whether to build it expected around 2028. An electron-positron ring does not need record-field magnets, but its proposed proton successor, FCC-hh, would. CERN's High Field Magnet program is targeting Nb3Sn dipoles with a 14 T operating field, and current FCC-hh parameter sets call for more than 4,400 dipoles . TechRadar first covered CERN's plans for a ring of that scale in 2019, when the FCC was still a conceptual design. That makes the HL-LHC's 30 quadrupoles the closest thing anyone has to a production run of Nb3Sn accelerator magnets. articles.title: New Nvidia bug is killing SSDs — is it “AI code incompetence,” users ask?
articles.content: If you haven't updated your Nvidia drivers recently, you may want to hold off. A newly discovered bug apparently can damage your PC by writing excessive amounts of data to solid-state drives (SSDs). The bug was found in the two most recent Nvidia GPU driver updates — specifically 621.14 and 621.24 — for the Nvidia GeForce Game Ready Driver. The 621.24 update was released on November 12. The bug was discovered by TroubleGrid who reported that the bug causes the NVDisplay.Container.exe to write (save data) far too much information to an Nvidia log file that can degrade the SSD. It can result in as much as 30GB per hour. The executable already wrote log files before the updates but not that much. SSDs typically take years to degrade, but the excessive data written by this bug can speed up the process causing stuttering and mouse lag. Conspiracy theories and Never Update On Reddit, I've seen a few posts about the bug with users complaining that this is why you never update. "By principle I never ever update my drivers unless there are feature inclusions for let's say a new game I bought," one Redditor said . Plenty of others agreed with that sentiment, and I'm inclined to say they're correct here. The other half of the comments split between blaming AI-written code. Before his ouster , CEO Jensen Huang was pushing for Nvidia engineers to use more AI-generated code via chatbots and agents. Or they were of the belief that Nvidia is purposely killing drives to force customers to pay more for new ones. Several called out Sam Altman and his recent claim that laptop RAM is a "terrible" allocation of a scarce resource. "I honestly would not be surprised if they are doing this on purpose to kill our NVMe's," wrote a poster. If we were to put blame on something, at this point, I'd say its AI-fueled incompetence, not AI-fueled greed, though that has led to said stupidity. How to avoid the bug (Image credit: Nvidia) The easiest fix is to rollback your graphics card driver to version 621.01, which is the last known patch to lack this bug. TroubleGrid listed a manual fix that requires you to set the Nvidia Display Container LS service to manual. Though it'll cost you. Basically, this can disable the Nvidia Control Panel and Nvidia App, meaning G-Sync color settings, display scaling, resolution overrides and more will not rock. "Do not disable the service outright if you use G-SYNC or a custom colour profile," the report warns. If you need a temporary fix, you can stop the service, delete the log file and start again. However, the file will return and continue to grow in size. articles.title: How Rockstar's animation makes GTA 6 a fully living and breathing world
articles.content: Rockstar Games told us about just how much effort went into the animation for GTA 6 That included work to get the right blend of pace and realism for the game, and a 'huge effort' with nailing all the details It also meant fleshing out 'close to a thousand animation sets for ambient activities' alongside layers of custom sequences and one-off events which are designed to reward those who fully explore the world Rockstar Games has underlined just how much work went into the gameplay animation side of GTA 6 in an effort to create a living and breathing world – and one that's rewarding to explore fully. TechRadar Gaming fired over a bunch of questions on the animation side of the game to Rockstar ahead of the release of GTA 6 , receiving some illuminating responses from two key developers at the company. Mike Jones, who is Director of Animation: Gameplay Animation, made it clear how the overall pacing of GTA 6 was finely tuned using animation, stressing how important it is to get the weight and feel of movement correct. Jones explained: "From the outset, we wanted to make the game feel fast and responsive yet maintain a weight which grounds our world in realism. Red Dead Redemption 2 had an appropriate slower heartbeat based on its setting. Jason and Lucia's world demands a faster pacing to interactions and movement." The level of detail that Rockstar's animators went into was also highlighted as a crucial part of pushing the GTA 6 experience to new heights of realism. Jones observed: "We put a huge effort into the details, which means teams caring about something as mundane as how the players might use a door when carrying drinks. Lucia may turn her back to open a door with her hip whilst her hands are occupied. That took months of development, but it matters." That painstaking level of detail is important for the action sequences too. Jones further noted: "Traversal is far more fluid than anything we've achieved before. We put significant effort into vaulting and climbing over obstacles and fences, always trying to maintain momentum. "There are countless variations depending on how the player triggers the action, the ability to branch out and chain together jumps and how they land. The amount of visual detail on the roofs of buildings is astounding, and the traversal allows for some breathtaking foot chases." Rewarding the curious (Image credit: Rockstar) As well as that sense of realism and pace, the animation team was fully engaged in making the world of GTA 6 something that you want to explore – an environment that rewards the player who wants to take the time to peek down that alley and investigate parts of the city that are more off the beaten path. Mark Tennant, who is Vice President of Animation at Rockstar, told us: "The sheer variety of animation required to flesh out the ambient world is staggering. Beyond the core human and animal locomotion needed to support the wide array of inhabitants, people hanging out and doing day-to-day jobs form the foundation of this living world. "There are close to a thousand animation sets for ambient activities, then we layer in hundreds of bespoke one-off events and custom sequences to punctuate the world and reward exploration." This was a "massive amount of data to manage" Tennant says, and it involved close collaboration with GTA 6's design team to keep things consistent across the game world. Even considering GTA 6 purely from a standpoint of the animation, it's clear how involved the production process was – and that Rockstar really wanted to nail getting the game right. Thankfully, as our review makes clear , Rockstar did just that, and the wait was very much worth it. If you're thinking of picking up the game, these are the cheapest ways to buy GTA 6 .

articles.title: 'Intel’s commitment to the HPC community is grounded in a pragmatic reality': Intel affirms its backing for the next generation of high-powered computing to push the boundaries of AI
articles.content: Intel's Diamond Rapids processors will feature up to 256 performance cores The upcoming Xeon architecture promises memory bandwidth reaching 1.6 TB/s Intel's GPU D-series accelerators will support up to 480GB LPDDR5X memory Intel is advancing its high-performance computing technologies through new Xeon processors, dedicated AI accelerators, and developments in optical connectivity and quantum computing. These investments are part of the company's strategy to support increasingly demanding scientific applications while allowing research institutions to retain existing software and computing infrastructure. Jeff McVeigh, Intel's vice president and general manager of Data Center Strategic Programs, says the company's approach prioritizes cooperation between different hardware and software technologies rather than dependence on a single computing architecture. Diamond Rapids and GPU D-series address computational demands Intel's forthcoming Diamond Rapids server processors will increase computing capacity through additional processing cores, expanded cache resources, and substantially higher memory throughput. The architecture will support configurations containing up to 256 performance cores, accompanied by memory bandwidth reaching 1.6 TB/s and last-level cache capacity of 1.28 GB. Additional capabilities include Intel Advanced Performance Extensions, AVX 10.2, and improved Advanced Matrix Extensions, providing hardware acceleration for demanding scientific calculations and artificial intelligence workloads. Intel says Diamond Rapids will extend the capabilities of its Xeon 6 processors, which support intensive simulation, mathematical modeling, and other computationally demanding applications. The company is also developing its GPU D-series for research organizations requiring substantial accelerator memory alongside artificial intelligence processing and double-precision mathematical computing capabilities. These accelerators will accommodate up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory, with supported numerical formats extending from FP4 and MXFP4 to FP64. Their conventional PCIe connectivity and air-cooled configuration are intended to simplify installation within existing computing facilities without requiring specialized cooling infrastructure. Greater onboard memory capacity could reduce repeated transfers between processors and accelerators, particularly when scientific applications handle extensive datasets or computationally demanding artificial intelligence models. Software compatibility, optical networking and quantum computing Beyond processor development, Intel is maintaining investments in software technologies that allow research institutions to retain existing applications while adopting newer computing architectures. Its software portfolio includes Intel MPI, Fortran compilers, optimization tools, and oneAPI, which support parallel applications across different hardware configurations. McVeigh argues that introducing faster processors becomes less useful when developers must abandon established applications or rewrite substantial amounts of existing software. Intel therefore intends to prepare software support alongside new hardware releases, allowing commonly used artificial intelligence frameworks and inference environments to operate immediately. This approach also supports hybrid scientific workflows in which conventional processors coordinate applications while accelerators undertake computationally intensive artificial intelligence operations. Intel is additionally pursuing silicon photonics to address communication limitations associated with moving information across increasingly large supercomputing installations. The technology uses optical signals instead of conventional electrical transmission, potentially reducing energy consumption and transmission delays as connections extend between processors, memory, and accelerators. Quantum computing represents another research direction, with Intel proposing to acquire…

articles.title: Skilled.dev Is Now Free and Open Source
articles.content: The interactive coding interview course is free to use, free to self-host, and open to contributions I built Skilled.dev 5 years ago based on my experience sitting on both sides of the table while interviewing at FAANG companies and hiring dozens of engineers. My goal is to help people land jobs they love where they can find meaning and purpose. Skilled.dev is now free and fully open source. That includes all 66 lessons, the 28 coding problems you can run in your browser, and the video walkthroughs, which are now hosted on YouTube. The code behind the site is MIT-licensed at github.com/leveluphq/skilled , so you can run your own copy or help improve this one. You don’t need to run your own copy to study. The hosted site at skilled.dev is free too. If you find it helpful, give the GitHub repo a star so others can more easily discover it. Interviews have changed a lot since I started the course, so I’ll start there. How interviews have changed with AI AI changed both what interviews test and how they test it, and companies went two ways. Some now hand you an AI. Canva expects candidates to use tools like Copilot, Cursor, and Claude in its technical interviews, and in that round it asks, “Can they identify and fix issues in AI-generated code?” Meta, Google, and Datadog have run AI-assisted rounds too, and interview platforms like CoderPad and HackerRank sell them to everyone else. Others take the AI away. Tools appeared that feed candidates answers during remote interviews without showing up on screen recordings, and some companies moved rounds back in person. Google gave fundamentals as its reason. Sundar Pichai said Google would add “at least one round of in-person interviews for people just to make sure the fundamentals are there.” Both kinds of rounds test fundamentals. One checks whether you can write the code without help, and the other checks whether you can tell when the AI’s code is wrong. I go through both, with examples, in Coding Interview Prep When Agents Write the Code . What the future may hold for interviews My guess is that both kinds of rounds stay. AI-assisted rounds will spread, because they match how engineers work now. Companies will keep at least one round without AI, because they need to know what you can do when the AI is wrong. More interviews will start from existing code, where you find the bug, add the feature, or make it faster. Algorithm questions will get harder to memorize, and what you’ve built on your own will count for more. Why fundamentals still matter Sean Goedecke wrote that “The most important skill in prompting is expertise in the domain you’re prompting for” ( LLMs reward expertise ). If you know data structures and algorithms, you can steer an AI toward a good solution and catch it when it’s wrong. If you don’t, you have to take what it gives you. Here’s one example from the deep dive. The brute-force answer to two-sum checks every pair of numbers: function twoSum(nums, target) { for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) { for (let j = i + 1; j < nums.length; j++) { if (nums[i] + nums[j] === target) return [i, j]; } } return null; } It’s correct, and with 1,000 numbers it finishes in under 2 milliseconds, so it passes a small test. With 100,000 numbers it takes 3.4 seconds. The version with a hash map takes 7.5 milliseconds. An AI can write either one in a second, and Big O is how you know which one you’re looking at. What Skilled.dev is Skilled.dev teaches what I’ve seen work in real coding interviews. The course covers 12 topics: arrays, Big O, hash tables, strings, recursion, searching and sorting, linked lists, stacks and queues, trees, graphs, dynamic programming, and JavaScript for frontend and Node roles. The topics most likely to come up, and the ones later topics build on, come first. Each topic has two parts. First, a lesson teaches the data structure or algorithm, and you implement it from scratch. Then you practice interview questions that use it. Each question starts with a…

articles.title: Get Amazon’s colour e-reader at its cheapest Aussie price yet — slashed to just AU$237 for Black Friday
articles.content: I've been the proud owner of a Kindle Colorsoft (2024) for over a year now, and it's truly changed my life for the better. And if you're in the market for one, I've got even better news for you — it's now hit its lowest-ever price in Australia in the Black Friday sales. As the brand's debut colour Kindle in 2024, it opened the doors for comic book and manga readers to enjoy their favourite novels digitally. In recent months, Amazon AU has expanded its multicolour lineup by introducing the Colorsoft (2026) , the Colorsoft Signature Edition (2026) and the Colorsoft Scribe (2026) , further cementing that colour Kindles are here to stay. And I'm all for it. • Shop all of Amazon's Black Friday deals here Even at full RRP, nabbing one of these colour Kindles isn't within reach for the average reader. That said, Amazon's Black Friday sale has tipped its hat to the Bookish community with a nice 47% discount on the O.G. Kindle Colorsoft. That knocks a massive AU$212 off the e-reader! Colorsoft (16GB): was $449 now $237 The Kindle Colorsoft is currently discounted by 47% during Amazon's Black Friday sale. Using a 7-inch E Ink display with support for over 4,000 colours, 16GB storage and up to eight weeks' battery life on a single charge, the Colorsoft is hard to pass up, especially if you mostly read comics, manga or graphic novels. Also discounted is the Colorsoft Signature Edition with 32GB storage for AU$379 , which also adds wireless charging to the mix. View Deal Achieving an impressive 4.5 stars in our review, we applauded the Colorsoft’s sharp and vibrant display. That missing half-star is due to the reviewer finding the e-reader "decidedly expensive," but now, with this 47% discount, that pricing issue is non-existent. Thanks to its display, you can also enjoy book covers, comics and graphic novels in all their vibrant glory. You don't have to read colour texts to take full advantage of the display — the monochrome performance is quite good — and I personally enjoy looking at my pretty fantasy book covers in all their glory. You'll need to act fast to secure this impressive deal — this Kindle Colorsoft discount won't stick around longer than Cyber Monday, which falls on November 30, 2026.

articles.title: Score TP-Link Archer with full Wi-Fi 7 support and 10 Gbps wired networking for incredible 55% off its regular price
articles.content: Internet connection speeds are consistently rising most everywhere in the world, and more than a few spots already have multi-gigabit service available. Making those kinds of speeds available throughout your house, however, requires a competent router that can handle both the high throughput and a fairly high number of connected devices. Enter the TP-Link Archer BE9500 Wi-Fi 7 router with 10 Gbps WAN, which, as of right now, is on sale at Best Buy for under a single Benjamin , at $89.99 — or under half its regular price of $199.99. Check out all the TP-Link Archer BE9500 for $89.99 at Best Buy. TP-Link networking gear has earned a good reputation with techies thanks to good reliability and offering great specs at quite affordable pricing, as is the case in point. Unlike some routers that outright lie about supporting WiFi 7, the Archer BE9500 actually has the magical combo that fully enables the power of the latest protocol: a 6 GHz band, along with Multi Link Operation (MLO) support. All-time low price The TP-Link Archer BE9500 is a full-featured Wi-Fi 7 router with full 6 GHz and MLO support and a 10 Gbps WAN port for high-speed internet connections. View Deal That grants the BE9500 an entire 9.5 Gbps of combined wireless bandwidth across all three frequencies, broadcast into the airwaves by six beam-forming antennas. For physical connections, there's one 10 Gbps WAN port, along with two 2.5 Gbps connectors for your big workstations or gaming rigs, and an additional two gigabit ports. As befits a modern router, the Archer BE9500 supports EasyMesh for wiring additional devices, as well as separate guest and internal networks for segregating IoT and other classes of devices. There are four VPN flavors on offer for acting as both a server and a client, including support for the modern WireGuard protocol. A USB port for connecting storage media, parental controls, automatic firmware upgrade, VLAN tagging, and miscellaneous features round out the main features. Get this router while stocks last, for only $89.99 at Best Buy .

articles.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
articles.content: When Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments became generally available in August 2026, agents could autonomously pay for paid APIs, MCP servers, and web content over open protocols like x402 and MPP with payment limits and full observability. Today we extend that autonomy to AWS Marketplace , so agents can discover and buy x402-enabled software, APIs, data, and content, and pay in USD on the agent developer’s AWS bill, removing the need for stablecoin wallets or API keys. Figure 1: Overview of AgentCore payments showing the new AWS Billing integration for purchasing on AWS Marketplace Developers can also configure and automate discovery through the AWS Marketplace connector in AgentCore Gateway . Existing guardrails carry over, developers can set spending limits and approved sellers using AgentCore policy, and the payment session cap is enforced by AgentCore payments, so an agent is unable to overspend. Transactions are auditable in AWS CloudTrail and AWS Cost Explorer . Because agent purchases run through AWS accounts on both sides, agentic purchasing meets the security and auditability enterprises expect. The x402 catalog on AWS Marketplace is expanding with a growing roster of trusted, verified sellers. Tavily, a live search provider for agentic commerce, is one of them: Agentic commerce isn’t just about giving agents the ability to pay. It’s about giving enterprises the confidence to let them. That conviction is driving Tavily’s collaboration with the AWS team on the design of Agentic Commerce. By bringing secure, x402 powered transactions to AWS Marketplace and connecting agents with trusted, KYC verified providers, AWS is laying the foundation for autonomous commerce at production scale. This is what enterprise ready agentic commerce looks like. — Rotem Weiss, Founder & CEO, Tavily What’s launching today Today’s launch adds AWS Billing as a payment option in AgentCore payments. An agent can now pay x402-enabled AWS Marketplace sellers per request, in USD, settling on their AWS bill. When an AWS Marketplace seller responds with 402 Payment Required, its response includes a signed quote for the purchase. With AWS Billing, the agent can forward the seller’s x402 response to AgentCore payments. AgentCore payments checks session budgets, then returns a payment token. The agent retries the request to the seller with the payment token included and receives a successful response. AWS bills the charge to the AWS account where Payment Manager is set up, and the charge appears on that account’s AWS bill. To set up AWS Marketplace purchasing, the developer creates a Payment Manager with an AWS Billing connector. The connector only requires you to set up a service-linked role to access AWS Marketplace. Then, for each task, developers can create a payment session with a spending limit and give the agent the session ID. An agent’s first purchase from a seller creates an agreement for the AWS account with that seller, and AWS Marketplace automatically tracks later purchases against it. Each product will then show up as an AWS Marketplace line item. If your organization uses Private Marketplace , agents can only buy the products it allows. In addition, to discover new sellers, we are launching a new AWS Marketplace connector in AgentCore Gateway . This optional integration helps agents find products and their endpoints. At launch, AWS Billing supports the x402 exact scheme, where the seller quotes a fixed price for each request. In this post, we walk through a research agent that discovers a tool, pays for a single request through AWS Billing, and answers with sources, with nothing set up in advance. We also provide an accompanying GitHub sample that you can use to evaluate the setup in your own AWS account. Sample walkthrough Suppose a financial analyst asks the agent what was announced about agentic payments this week. The model wasn’t trained on this week’s news, so the agent looks for a search tool. Through AgentCore Gateway, it searches…

articles.title: Nvidia Approaches Arm Boss Rene Haas In Search For New CEO
articles.content: Nvidia has reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as it searches for a replacement for co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned last week amid a personal scandal. According to Bloomberg, Haas is emerging as a leading contender for the job. The 64-year-old previously worked at Nvidia as general manager of its computing products business before joining Arm, giving him firsthand experience with the AI chip giant. The Guardian reports: Heidrick & Struggles, the recruiting firm hired by the company's board, has started contacting potential candidates, according to Bloomberg. It reported that Rene Haas, who joined Arm in 2013 and became chief executive in 2022, is among those approached. [...] Haas, 64, is viewed as the leading contender for the top job at Nvidia, having previously worked at the $3.6tn company for seven years as the general manager of its computing products. Reports suggest that other potential candidates include: Ian Buck, an Nvidia vice-president; Lisa Su, AMD's chief executive; and Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer. Arm, which is listed in New York but retains its global headquarters in Cambridge, has about 500 users of its chip designs worldwide, including Nvidia, Apple, Samsung and Qualcomm. The company employs more than 7,000 staff, including more than 3,000 in the UK. It is the biggest tech firm headquartered in Britain, now valued at $196bn. Haas told a tech conference in Austin on Wednesday that Huang was "a legend." "What he built at Nvidia is historic," he said. "You don't have many champions like that." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Apple is Building an AI Agent That Can Use Apps and Code
articles.content: Apple is working on a proactive AI agent like Meta's Muse or OpenAI's Dots, according to job listings spotted by Bloomberg . The listing describes an AI agent that can code, use apps, and browse the web. Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we're looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real. Apple's listing notes that safety, privacy, and security need to be "central to the design" of its agentic AI. Apple is seeking someone who can work across the Siri , UI frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models teams, joining a group already working on "general-purpose computer-use agents." People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service. We're building AI agents that can do the same. We're a team of engineers, AI applied researchers, and systems specialists working on general-purpose computer-use agents. These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way. Bloomberg previously said Apple was aiming to make ‌Siri‌ "more like an agent" as soon as 2027. With almost every major AI company adopting proactive AI, it makes sense that Apple is rushing to create a competitive product. Meta came out with its Muse agent in September, and the app quickly shot up the App Store charts. OpenAI followed with Dots, Anthropic launched Claude Duet, and Google turned its Gemini Spark agent into "Tasks" and added new features. All of the proactive agents offer to do tasks for users without being asked, which isn't something ‌Siri‌ AI is capable of. New Apple CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing software engineering chief Craig Federighi to move faster on AI. articles.title: Gemini could soon make it easy to find chats where you left unfinished draft text
articles.content: TL;DR Google is working on indicators to show when you’ve left a draft message in Gemini chats. Users would be able to filter the chat list to only show those with active drafts. Gemini’s also working on new tools for sharing chat output and Live prompts. Working with an AI as powerful as Gemini can be a little overwhelming — where do you even start, with so many options available to you — and if you frequently find yourself leaving things hanging before you finish sharing your latest thoughts with Gemini, you just might appreciate what looks like a new feature for managing your drafts. We’ve uncovered evidence for just that, as well as new tools for sharing your Gemini sessions, in a recent app update. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. Gemini already saves drafts that you’ve started writing but have yet to submit. The problem right now is that there’s no good way to find them. If you pull up your list of past chats, when you tap on one you’ll see any draft text still in the box, but there’s no way to know that’s there from your main list of chats in the app’s menu.

articles.title: Seven Spheres Became an App: Here's How
articles.content: There is a photograph I took in 2017, on the floor of a university library, of an open copy of Jonathan Black's The Secret History of the World . The page is the one where Black describes the planetary sequence: Saturn, the Sun, Venus, the Moon, and Jupiter, weaving the conditions that made life on Earth possible. I remember taking it because I wanted to remember the exact page. I did not think anything further about what I would do with it. Nine years later, I opened my laptop this morning to an analytics dashboard for a piece of software I have been building for two years. Forty-three thousand people visited the site last month. Most of them came in through articles in the grimoire, a knowledge base I have built out to roughly two thousand entries on planetary correspondences, crystals, herbs, spells, runes, tarot, and the relationships between them. The library, and the dashboard. Twenty-one and twenty-nine. Six years apart. I have only recently been able to say, out loud, that these are the same project. Why the MA did not end. Most MA research ends at graduation. You hand in the thesis, the external examiners sign off, the degree is conferred, and the research becomes a document you put in a drawer. That is not a failure mode; that is what most research is for. It proves you can do the work, and then you stop. Mine did not stop, because the research had planted a question I could not answer with more reading. It was something like: if the Hermetic cosmology is internally coherent across two thousand years of texts, across Egyptian and Greek and Latin and Coptic translation, across Black and Mead and Everard and Freke and Gandy, and if it describes a specific mechanism by which consciousness enters a body through seven planetary spheres, then what would that mechanism look like rendered in software? I did not have a coherent answer at 23. I did not even know I was asking the question. I knew I had painted invisible sentences onto the inside walls of a cube. I knew I thought the Wordsworth line was the most important sentence I had ever read. I knew something in the Corpus Hermeticum had landed with me and would not leave. When I started building Lunary in May 2024, I was not thinking about the MA. I was thinking about a technical problem: existing astrology platforms were either dated, credulous, or marketed as entertainment, and I believed there was room for something that took the underlying system seriously. It was only about six months in, writing the knowledge schema for the grimoire, that I realised I was building the thesis I had written at 22. In code this time, and in Postgres tables, and in the way the birth chart calculator consumed a VSOP87 ephemeris and turned it into a set of quality assignments. Same argument. Different medium. What Lunary actually is, read through the MA lens. Here is what Lunary is, if you read it through the Hermetic frame I spent nine months in the library building. The birth chart is the record of the qualities your consciousness acquired as it descended through the seven spheres. That is the reading Parts 4 and 5 of this series made explicit: the soul descends through Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, picking up a signature quality from each sphere, and the configuration at birth is the local snapshot of that descent. The chart is not a prediction. It is a receipt. Lunary's chart module calculates the positions using astronomy-engine, an open-source VSOP87 implementation in JavaScript, under an MIT licence. No subscription is needed to see the chart. It is the most honest object in the product. The transit engine is the ongoing conversation between your acquired qualities and the spheres that gave them to you. When Mars moves across the position where the Moon sat at your birth, something that the ancient cosmology would call a conversation is happening between the sphere that contributed your instinct and reflex and the sphere that contributed your capacity for…

articles.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
articles.content: When hundreds of agents serve thousands of developers, enterprise governance can’t be an afterthought. At the BMW Group’s R&D, more than 12,500 developers work on approximately 500 million lines of vehicle software code. This software is augmented by the BMW Connected Vehicle backend, a cloud-based system of more than 1,300 microservices providing digital services for 24 million vehicles in the field. In regulated industry, the bar for (software) quality, stability, and governance compliance is exceptionally high. While research, frameworks, and guidelines now facilitate building agents, industrializing and operating high-quality agents in an efficient, scalable manner remains a significant challenge. Scaling agentic AI across a large organization cannot be achieved by isolated teams. It requires collective effort, locally driven experimentation, and active knowledge sharing across the enterprise. This creates a fundamental governance dichotomy: Development teams need the freedom to innovate rapidly, while the enterprise must enforce standards for safety, security, composability, and cost-efficiency. Without that balance, organizations risk a fragmented landscape of AI islands and costly duplicate work. This presents a real challenge given hundreds of globally distributed teams building agents across the BMW Group. In this post, we detail the practices and patterns that support BMW’s R&D teams in building, governing and operating agents at scale without sacrificing speed, quality or compliance. Solution Our premise is straightforward: build agents that can cooperate from the start. This requires an architecture that makes diversity composable, governable, and automatable, without requiring a single framework or toolchain. Central to this architecture is the agent harness, a runtime layer wrapped around a large language model (LLM). It provides the execution loop, tool dispatch, memory management, and observability hooks for autonomous operation. Just as the AWS Well-Architected Framework standardized cloud infrastructure design, agentic systems need equivalent patterns, reusable blueprints encoding governance, composability, and operational best practices from the start. We organize our solution around five interlocking practices, drawn from hands-on experience building and operating agentic systems at enterprise scale since 2023. Each practice is codified as infrastructure as code (IaC), making adoption repeatable, auditable, and enforceable across teams without blocking DevOps velocity. Govern proactively, not retroactively Governance must be structural from the start and maintained across the full lifecycle. We advocate for three properties of effective agentic governance: Framework-agnostic and externalized: Governance rules such as authentication, authorization, rate limiting and content filtering are enforced at the integration layer. This includes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway, a central agent registry and orchestration boundary, rather than within individual agent codebases. This means governance survives framework migrations, model swaps, and team reorganizations. Domain-sensitive and graduated: Not every agent action carries the same risk: drafting documentation, updating customer records, and production database writes demand very different levels of oversight. We implement graduated trust through per-step autonomy levels: Level 0 (Human-in-the-loop): Every action requires explicit human approval. This is the starting point for new agents and high-risk operations. Level 1 (Human-on-the-loop): The agent executes autonomously but surfaces decisions for asynchronous human review. Suitable for medium-risk tasks with defined inputs, outputs, and rollback options. Level 2 (Autonomous within guardrails): The agent operates independently within strictly defined policy boundaries, enforced deterministically rather than through prompt instructions (see below). Reserved for low-risk, well-understood operations with…

articles.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
articles.content: Most sellers do not need another AI product to learn. They need the tools and information they already use brought together, so they can see what is happening in their business and act on it. AWS Quick and the Amazon Selling Partner plugin do that together. Quick brings an Amazon seller’s sales data, inventory signals, and marketplace intelligence into one place, where questions become answers and answers become actions. It understands the seller’s full business context, so the seller does not need to re-explain their catalog, their margins, or their competitive landscape in every conversation. It is built on AWS, the same infrastructure Amazon uses to run its own marketplace. At Amazon Accelerate on September 23, 2026, Amazon announced the Selling Partner plugin and launched it in beta in AWS Quick. This post covers what launched, how to claim the free AWS Quick offer, and what the experience looks like day to day. It also covers how the skills and connectors work when a seller puts them to use. Limited-time offer: 12 months of AWS Quick Plus, free. Every primary selling account holder worldwide can claim a free 12-month subscription, plus access for 10 additional users you delegate. Sign up by December 31, 2026. Claim your free AWS Quick Plus offer. 1. Why Quick is right for Amazon sellers Four things make Quick a fit for how Amazon sellers already work: it learns the business, it reaches beyond the Amazon store, it turns data into decisions, and it protects seller data on infrastructure sellers already trust. Quick knows your business, not only your prompts Quick and the Selling Partner plugin connect to a seller’s inventory feeds, sales data, and operational documents. From these, Quick builds a living understanding of the catalog structure, margin thresholds, seasonality, and competitive position. Ask Quick to audit your ASINs for Q4, and it returns a ranked recommendation built on the seller’s real margin data, historical conversion, and inventory availability. Its recommendations get sharper the more the seller works with it. Quick does not stop at your Amazon store A seller’s business runs across many tools: a storefront on another channel, an email inbox, an accounting system, spreadsheets, a supplier portal. Quick connects to where the seller already works and pulls context from across the whole operation. It is a business assistant that happens to know Amazon deeply, so the seller grows overall, not on one channel alone. It turns data into decisions you can act on Sellers are not short on data. They have Brand Analytics, Search Query Performance, advertising reports, inventory health, and listing quality data. The problem is turning those signals into one clear action. Quick does the synthesis. It watches for change, flags what matters, builds the analysis, and presents the decision with the evidence behind it. Your data stays protected on the infrastructure you already sell on Quick runs on AWS and does not use seller data to train models, not for general improvement and not for anything else. Seller data stays in the seller’s environment and never informs anyone else’s models. For a seller already operating on the Amazon marketplace, there is no new security posture to evaluate. The infrastructure is the same one protecting the seller account today, and the seller’s chosen AWS Region governs where data stays. The Amazon Selling Partner plugin The Selling Partner plugin connects AWS Quick directly to live Seller Central data. After one sign-in with a Seller Central account, the plugin gives conversational access to product listings, inventory, and sales data, pulled live rather than exported and reassembled by hand. It installs like an app, with no coding required. It ships with curated Amazon skills, and it pairs with Amazon Ads MCP so campaign performance and spend sit next to the selling data. The plugin is in beta for US stores. Figure 1: The Selling Partner plugin consent screen, where the seller grants None,…

articles.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code
articles.content: The data and code that underpin a research study can tell us what was actually done, and how. In a medical study, for example, how were patients selected for inclusion? How were missing values handled? How were the results evaluated? Access to a study's data and code help researchers to answer these questions, to examine the methods, and to build on the work. “Studies involve many choices about how to prepare data, develop models, and evaluate performance. These are sometimes called ‘researcher degrees of freedom,’” says Tom Pollard, a research scientist at MIT's Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. “The choices we make affect the results, and a methods section in a paper can only capture so much detail.” While sharing code can be a first step, in order for code to be understood and reused, it must be sufficiently structured and described. The problem is that, right now, there is little guidance for researchers on what constitutes a well-organized, well-described collection of code. This is where an international team led by researchers at MIT and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute sought to help, by examining how code is currently shared in clinical prediction studies. Such studies develop or evaluate models to estimate patient outcomes, such as the risk of developing a disease. Because these models inform decisions about patient care, researchers need to be able to scrutinize how they were built and tested. Using large language models (LLMs), the researchers examined nearly 4,000 papers to identify statements about shared code. They then followed the statements to assess hundreds of associated code repositories. Their review revealed two key gaps: Code sharing remains uncommon, and making code public does not consistently mean providing the documentation and supporting information needed for reuse. The open-access findings, recently published in Nature Medicine , are informing TRIPOD-Code , a reporting guideline being developed to clarify what researchers should share. Following the code TRIPOD-Code builds on TRIPOD and TRIPOD+AI, checklists that help researchers report how clinical prediction models were developed and evaluated. To understand current code-sharing practices, the team identified studies citing either guideline. The review included almost 4,000 studies that developed, updated, or validated prediction models, and whose full texts were available through PubMed Central’s open-access collection. “The challenge was that the information was highly inconsistent. First, we had to identify whether or not a paper shared code” says Thomas Sounack, the study’s first author. He adds that authors “discuss and link to code from a paper in many different ways.” The team used an LLM to help screen papers, identify statements about code availability, and extract links. Software then retrieved the linked repositories — online collections of code and related files — for further assessment. The workflow went beyond checking whether a link existed. It also assessed repositories against characteristics such as completeness of documentation, software requirements, and terms of reuse. “The real benefit of LLMs is their ability to process unstructured information such as text. These models helped us work with information that was scattered across papers and software repositories, rather than neatly organized in a table,” says Pollard, who is a senior author of the study. “That allowed us to examine how code was being shared in much more detail across a large collection of studies.” Human reviewers evaluated the work of the LLMs. Two researchers independently checked 500 papers and a separate sample of repositories, resolving disagreements before comparing their assessments with the automated results. Agreement was stronger for concrete characteristics, such as whether a license file was present, than for judgments about the adequacy of documentation. Because classification…

articles.title: 53% of Gamers Rank Black Friday as the Best Value Event of the Year, Reveals New G2A.COM Survey
articles.content: Amsterdam, Netherlands, November 19th, 2026/TechnologyWire/-- G2A.COM , the world’s largest marketplace for digital entertainment, has polled just over 2,000 of its users to investigate whether Black Friday still plays a crucial role in the annual purchasing journey. The findings reveal that, beyond the appeal of discounts, players are making increasingly deliberate purchasing decisions, tracking prices and postponing purchases in anticipation of Black Friday. This follows a recent report by Newzoo and G2A.COM, titled Game purchasing behavior in an era of choice , which provided a detailed examination of how gamers are dealing with higher prices, their attitudes toward discounts, and the growing number of ways to buy games. Key Findings: Gamers Plan Their Purchases Around Black Friday: Over half of those surveyed (53%) identify Black Friday and Cyber Monday as offering the best value for game purchases, significantly outpacing routine seasonal storefront sales (7%) and publisher-specific sales (2%). Waiting for Black Friday Influences Purchasing Decisions: 64% of respondents have delayed buying games or in-game content released between September and November to wait for Black Friday discounts, including 38.6% who do so frequently and 25.5% occasionally. Meanwhile, 19% said they buy games immediately if they want them at launch. When it comes to planning ahead, 17% typically hold off on purchases for one to two weeks, another 17% for around a month, and 22% for two months or longer. Full Games Drive Purchase Plans: When asked which products they wait until Black Friday to purchase, 87% of respondents selected full games, followed by expansions and DLC (36%), subscriptions (26%) and in-game currency (18%). Tracking Prices with Wishlists and Marketplaces: Store wishlist notifications (e.g., Steam, PlayStation Store, Xbox) emerged as the primary tool for deal discovery, with 55% of respondents relying on them. Digital marketplaces like G2A.COM are the second-most-popular channel at 47%, beating dedicated price-tracking sites (29%). G2A.COM’s transactional data reinforces the commercial importance of this shopping period. During Black Friday–Cyber Monday 2025, total orders in the marketplace increased by 33% year-on-year, while video game orders surged by 87%, significantly outpacing overall growth. G2A.COM’s survey findings reveal that, despite a growing trend of delayed purchases and consumer skepticism, Black Friday remains the peak value event for gamers. This data corroborates with the recent Newzoo report, which found that 73% of gamers feel AAA games are overpriced at launch and, on average, wait 4.9 months for a sale or discount. Together, the studies highlight how price awareness and patience increasingly influence purchasing decisions, with Black Friday proving a key opportunity for gamers to act on their plans. "Black Friday is no longer just about impulse purchases. It has become a planned part of how gamers manage their entertainment budgets," said Paweł Wróbel, Chief Growth Officer at G2A.COM. "Players are increasingly willing to wait, track prices and prioritise the games they want most. Our findings show that getting the best value is becoming just as important as getting a game at launch." The survey further reveals that 39% of respondents plan to spend more on gaming this Black Friday than last year, while 41% expect to spend roughly the same amount. These findings underline Black Friday’s continued importance as a major shopping period for gamers, increasingly shaped by preparation, informed decisions and the search for value. About G2A.COM G2A.COM is the world's largest marketplace for digital entertainment, serving over 35 million users from 180 countries with more than 200 million visits in 2025. articles.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Disclose Cyberattack On Third-Party Vendors
articles.content: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed cyberattacks involving third-party service providers that exposed customer marketing data, including names, email addresses and, in some cases, phone numbers and postal codes. All three companies said their core systems or payment networks were unaffected, while JPMorgan emphasized that the incident was unrelated to the banking disruptions earlier this week. Reuters reports: A cyber extortion group called "n0n" claimed on November 16 to have obtained cardmember engagement records that included "hundreds of thousands of campaign interactions for tens of thousands of distinct cardmember email addresses," according to a screenshot of the message captured by cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The data includes what appears to be 124 bank employee email addresses and more than 16,000 customer email addresses, some with phone numbers and postal codes, according to a Reuters review. Reuters could not independently verify the authenticity of the data. The same hacking group on November 16 posted similar claims regarding Visa and Mastercard and posted data. [...] The Mastercard data posted by n0n includes marketing data related to customers in North America, the Middle East and Africa, and a small number of Mastercard employee email addresses. The hacking group has claimed roughly 200 incidents since emerging in September 2026, according to eCrime.ch. "Customers don't distinguish between a bank and a vendor when it comes to a cyberattack, so there is a question of reputational risk here," said Carissa Robb at SolomonEdwards, a consulting firm. "There needs to be a little bit more pressure on how often companies are scrutinizing the amount of data that is shared with vendors and the necessity of the data being shared," Robb said. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
