articles.title: Jensen Huang Chinese Revenue, Affairs, Resignation, and Case for CEO Reinstatement Timeline
articles.content: The first NVIDIA earnings call after Jensen Huang’s departure opened with the answer to a question Silicon Valley had spent the weekend asking. The board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” chair Harvey Jones said. Earlier that day, Huang had said he would be “honored” to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders and employees. Then interim CEO Colette Kress got to the numbers. NVIDIA had just booked $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue , including $11.05 billion from direct customers headquartered in China and Hong Kong . NVIDIA’s decision on reinstatement · Jensen Huang’s comeback statement · NVIDIA’s geographic revenue disclosure A third number came out on the call. NVIDIA sold $2.4 billion of licensed Hopper data-center products to China in the quarter. Kress said those shipments had stopped and the company’s next-quarter guidance excluded them. The economics get harder to trace when a Chinese business rents computing power abroad or when NVIDIA hardware reaches an end user through intermediaries. Licensed Hopper sales and the shipment halt · NVIDIA’s definition of indirect customers The original HackerNoon Jensen Huang affair timeline followed his public remarks, the Singapore cloud company Megaspeed, and his admission of infidelity. The ensuing days brought reports of two relationships with NVIDIA employees, a resignation that cost Huang his board seat as well as his job, a campaign to bring him back, and a U.S. rule aimed at Chinese access to advanced computing overseas. The dates matter. NVIDIA’s SEC filing records the board accepting his resignation on November 11 . The company told the public on November 12 . Reuters on the second NVIDIA employee · NVIDIA’s resignation filing · Federal Register rule on remote computing How much revenue does NVIDIA get from China? NVIDIA used to assign revenue geographically by the address on the bill. In Q3 FY2026 it switched to the headquarters of the direct customer and recast earlier figures. A company can be invoiced in Singapore, be headquartered elsewhere, take delivery in Malaysia, and rent computing capacity to a business in China. Each is a different fact about the transaction. NVIDIA’s newer tables answer the headquarters question. The older ones answer the billing question. The region’s share of total revenue still fell over those nine months because NVIDIA’s overall business grew faster. The geography line covers multiple product categories, while Kress’s $2.4 billion figure describes licensed Hopper data-center products specifically. Adding the latter to the former would mix two views of overlapping sales. articles.title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
articles.content: Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to…

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks Signs $4.5 Billion Deal For Applied Compute
articles.content: Palo Alto Networks has agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion as it expands beyond traditional cybersecurity into securing enterprise AI systems, including the training and deployment of open-weight models. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Reuters reports: Palo Alto Networks has been repositioning itself as an integrated cybersecurity provider, with recent deals, including its $3.35 billion acquisition of cloud management and monitoring firm Chronosphere and an agreement with Israeli startup Koi. The company is looking to tap growing cybersecurity spending as the rapid adoption of AI creates new security risks and gives attackers new ways to exploit vulnerabilities. "AI tools are surfacing vulnerabilities faster than companies can patch them, and that is pushing customers to consolidate onto fewer platforms," said Catharine Trebnick, senior research analyst at Rosenblatt Securities. With the acquisition of Applied Compute, Palo Alto aims to offer a technology platform that helps customers securely train and deploy open-weight models as they expand their use of AI. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Nvidia adds possible hack to list of very bad things under investigation
articles.content: Finding a new CEO is just one of their problems. Nvidia is investigating an alleged breach following claims by ransomware group The Gentlemen's affiliates that they hacked the AI giant and stole sensitive information. The embattled chipmaker told The Register 's that it was investigating a possible third-party data breach. “We have found no indication that Nvidia systems or networks were affected,” a spokesperson said. “We continue to monitor the situation." The ransomware gang’s data-leak site, shared on social media and seen by The Register , doesn’t show any stolen files or indicate what information the group claims to have stolen. Nvidia first appeared on the criminals’ blog on Wednesday, with The Gentlemen promising “DATA INFO - SOON.” The post also included a countdown, ending November 28. While we can’t verify the criminals’ claims, the group, which emerged in mid-2025 , is one of the most prolific ransomware-as-a-service operations. Its affiliates claimed more than 320 victims as of April, with the majority of these alleged ransomware infections (240) occurring in the first half of 2026. The actual count, however, is likely much higher. Check Point researchers accessed an affiliate’s live command-and-control server during an incident response case earlier this year. The server contained victim telemetry that revealed more than 1,570 victims , mostly located in the US, and primarily corporate and organizational environments. According to an operational technology (OT) threat report from Trellix published on Wednesday, industrial ransomware claims jumped nearly 51 percent - to about 1,500 posts- compared to last quarter, and The Gentlemen’s affiliates were the most prolific claim posters during this time period. They accounted for about 16 percent of all posts. In February 2022, an Nvidia data breach exposed employees’ credentials and proprietary code. Extortion crew Lapsus$ claimed to be responsible for that intrusion and data theft.®

articles.title: iPhone Duo vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8: Which is Better?
articles.content: A couple of months before the iPhone Duo came out, Samsung launched the Galaxy Z Fold8. It's Samsung's widest and shortest foldable to date, with Samsung adopting an aspect ratio closer to the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s than its previous foldable smartphones. Since the Z Fold8 was clearly designed to compete with the ‌iPhone Duo‌, we thought we'd compare the two devices. Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos. The Galaxy Z Fold8 and ‌iPhone Duo‌ are similar in size, but the Fold8 is noticeably lighter. It's about 50 grams lighter than the ‌iPhone Duo‌, and it makes a difference when you're holding it. It's lighter because it's thinner than the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when folded and unfolded. The Z Fold8 is 6mm taller and around 3mm narrower, though both have a 7.6-inch inner display. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ has a heftier feel and a more premium build, plus it has rounded corners that feel nicer in the hand than the Z Fold8's sharper, rectangular corners. Apple used a matte nano-texture display for the ‌iPhone Duo‌, and that's likely something we're going to see Android smartphone makers imitate in their future foldables. The matte display goes a long way toward minimizing the visibility of the crease. Apple also put the camera on the inner display under the screen, which is something Samsung experimented with in earlier models and then abandoned. Under-display front cameras are generally lower resolution than standard cameras, and there have been complaints about the quality of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s inner front camera. The Z Fold8 has a more traditional hole-punch camera that's better quality. Both smartphones use fingerprint recognition rather than facial recognition, but Samsung has long offered a face unlock feature that uses the front-facing camera. Apple just this week adopted a similar face unlock option , and it's coming in iOS 27.3. Face unlock is less secure than the Face ID system used for Apple's other iPhones, but it is more convenient than Touch ID for some users. Neither smartphone has a telephoto camera, so both Apple and Samsung compromised on camera quality. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ has a 48-megapixel Main camera and a 48-megapixel Ultra Wide, while the Z Fold8 has 50-megapixel wide and ultra wide cameras. The main difference in image quality is the computational processing each smartphone offers, so which one is "better" comes down to your preference for white balance, saturation, tone, and similar factors. The Z Fold8 supports 8K video recording and reverse wireless charging for accessories, plus it has a physical SIM while the Duo only has an eSIM. Samsung's smartphone is limited to IP48 dust and water resistance, while the ‌iPhone Duo‌ has IP68. Samsung uses the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, and the ‌iPhone Duo‌ has Apple's A20 Pro chip. The other big difference is stylus support. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ works with the USB-C Apple Pencil , but the Z Fold8 doesn't work with Samsung's S Pen options. Since Samsung has been making foldable smartphones for years, developers have had more time to update their apps for the form factor. Most Android apps already work well, while we're still waiting for many developers to update their apps for the Duo. Samsung is also ahead on multitasking, with the option to use three apps at once and support for pop-up windows and a taskbar. Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8 is slightly cheaper than the ‌iPhone Duo‌, with pricing starting at $1,899.99 while the Duo starts at $1,999, but deciding between them will come down to your operating system preference and device ecosystem. If you're accustomed to iOS and have an Apple Watch, Mac, and other Apple devices, there's little reason to choose a Samsung smartphone. The same goes for Samsung users who have other Galaxy devices. Do you prefer the ‌iPhone Duo‌ or the Galaxy Z Fold8? Let us know in the comments below.…

articles.title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
articles.content: Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change. But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen. It is served ephemerally to individual users, confined to their chat session. A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) tried to tackle this question from multiple angles, testing LLMs with different prompts and evaluating their output. They started with benchmarks of simple factual questions (benchmarks that might even be in models’ training data at this point) but also analyzed more complex interactions—including when users think they’re right to push back on an answer. CO 2 Q&A LLM research often faces ( no-true-Scotsman-tinged ) criticism for focusing on a particular model rather than some other frontier model that may have been released after the experiment concluded. In this case, the study used 33 models, including multiple versions of the major frontier and open-weight models. The flagship frontier models used were Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and GPT-5.6 Sol. (You can find the full list in the report .) articles.title: XXRI-OS explores the lowest end of the Linux desktop
articles.content: New Linux distros seem to appear daily, but far too few distinguish themselves by being smaller and simpler. XXRI OS is a fairly new desktop Linux distro. It has a snazzy-looking website, complete with an amusing URL, and along similar lines, its GitHub page has a very heavily formatted README. Nonetheless, this is not another over-complex opinionated slopfest of an OS with built-in AI, bizarre keystrokes, and several proprietary components. It's almost the reverse. The main download is just 287.4 MB, and that's the full distro, not a minimalist installer that fetches most of the OS over your internet connection. We installed it in a VirtualBox VM. It took 675 MB of disk space, and in the graphical desktop, when we opened a terminal window, it reported just 75 MB of RAM in use with the desktop and terminal running. We are restraining ourselves hard when we say that those are unusually low numbers for the 2020s. We would expect most cut-down lightweight Linux distros to use around five to 10 times as much disk space or memory. The current release of XXRI-OS is version 2.7. XXRI OS 1.0 came out in May 2025, making this a young project with five published releases already behind it. It also has much deeper roots: it is based on the existing and much older Tiny Core Linux . The Reg FOSS desk last looked at Tiny Core Linux 15 back in March 2024 and the project is still going strong: the latest version is version 17.1. Tiny Core Linux is a marvel, but there are prices to pay for somehow getting a graphical Linux desktop into a 23 MB download. It runs from RAM and uses its own extension-based package system, which can make adding components and managing updates unfamiliar territory. XXRI OS takes TCL and turns it into a slightly more conventional desktop. It installs to disk in the usual way, and it includes the core functions that most people would expect from their OS in 2026. It has a file manager, a text editor, a media player, a simple app store for adding further components, and a settings app including an update manager. It even includes its own web browser, and there are both x86-32 and x86-64 variants. The desktop layout has a floating dock at bottom center, and the icons are unlabelled. To save you some guesswork, though, floating just to the left of the dock is an icon with a grid of dots, which is an app launcher. The icons in that do have text labels underneath, so you can learn which symbol denotes which function from here. We plan to experiment more with this remarkable little OS and see how well it runs on the oldest, slowest boxes in the Irish Sea wing of Vulture Towers, but we like what we see so far. It's an impressive experiment in how low Linux can go and remain useful. While Tiny Core Linux goes down to Windows 95 levels of resource usage, XXRI OS has a more usable Windows 2000-level baseline. Over a quarter of a century later, that is nearly unbeatable. ®

articles.title: “Be ready for change”: AAIF’s CTO on why the agent stack won’t settle
articles.content: If you’ve spent any time over the past year trying to get AI agents to talk to each other without tearing your architecture apart, you know the struggle: vendor lock-in, fragmented protocols, and context that definitely vanishes the second you attempt to make a cross-framework handoff. It’s astounding how fast developers’ needs have changed just in 10 months since the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) was formed to help solve those problems. The Linux Foundation-backed AAIF gives shared agent infrastructure a home outside any one vendor’s control. It launched in December 2025 with three projects, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which connects AI applications to external tools and data. On October 22 , Anthropic contributed Agent Skills, and OpenAI contributed Open Responses to the foundation, alongside projects from Hugging Face and Alibaba. The additions brought AAIF to 10 hosted projects. The New Stack Editor-in-Chief Nick Lucchesi sat down with Manik Surtani , AAIF’s co-founder and CTO, for The New Stack podcast at AGNTCon + MCPCon in San Jose, shortly after Surtani announced the additions in his October 22 keynote. The news was still fresh — the problems behind it, though, were all too familiar. “I think that’s always been there,” Surtani said of the needs these projects address. “We’ve always known that sandboxes are really important.” Agent Skills, too, was already in use before joining the foundation. What had changed was where these projects would be governed. “…having a standardized way to speak to a model is super important.” “I’m really happy [Agent Skills] is here. And Open Responses as well. I mean, having a standardized way to speak to a model is super important. And I’m glad to see that it’s now happening in a way that is vendor-neutral, in a neutral governance and everything else.” Four giant projects join the foundation The big news from Surtani was this: Four heavy-hitting projects had joined the AAIF. Here’s what each brings to the table: Agent Skills (Anthropic): An open format for bundling instructions, scripts, and reference materials that an agent can load when it needs to perform a particular task. Write those instructions once, and use them across agents that support the format. Open Responses (OpenAI): An open specification, based on OpenAI’s Responses API, for how applications send requests to language models and receive results. A shared format means less translation work when developers switch between compatible model providers. OpenEnv (Hugging Face): A framework for building and sharing reinforcement learning environments, where agents practice tasks and receive feedback that can be used to train them. OpenSandbox (Alibaba): A platform for running agent-generated code and other work in isolated environments, separating that execution from the surrounding system. While Anthropic, OpenAI, Hugging Face, and Alibaba rallying around a neutral foundation sounds like an AI miracle, Surtani noted that developer demand for open governance has existed from Day 1. “More than faster, I think people are going to be able to build on top of things that they can trust more.” “More than faster, I think people are going to be able to build on top of things that they can trust more,” Surtani said. “It’s not like you couldn’t trust open responses before. Of course you could. But now everyone has a say in how it’s going to grow and how it’s going to get shaped.” Developers learned this lesson the hard way during the early cloud-native boom. Nobody wants to build core enterprise infrastructure on tech they can’t help steer. Tackling the real pain points: Agent memory and portability What problem keeps Surtani up at night? In the near term, it’s agent memory and context management — the information an…

articles.title: Google Meet is making it easy to download a local copy of the file your host’s presenting
articles.content: TL;DR Google is adding direct download support to Meet for files shared by presenters. Presenters can link to Google Docs, Sheets, or Slide files they screen-share with call participants. Sharing can be enabled only for specific files, or everything across the call. By now, we’ve all probably sat through at least one videoconference where we struggled to follow along with someone presenting a document like a slideshow or PDF, wishing we just had our own copy of the file to look at — and thankfully, Google Meet is now making it a lot easier for us to get our hands on just that. When a presenter screen-shares a document with the rest of the call, so far Meet hasn’t offered a built-in way to easily distribute copies of that document to call participants. Maybe the best option there has been just dropping a link in chat.

articles.title: 13 Best Agent Gateways in 2026 for MCP, A2A and LLM Traffic: Kong, Bifrost, AgentCore, Arcade
articles.content: Agents no longer just call a model. They call tools over MCP, delegate to other agents over A2A, and act inside business systems. The best agent gateways sit on that path and decide who can do what. This list compares 13 of them on traffic coverage, identity, deployment and price. What is an agent gateway? An agent gateway is a control point that authenticates agents, filters the tools they see, and logs every call. A plain LLM gateway only routes model requests. An agent gateway adds MCP tool governance, agent identity and, increasingly, A2A traffic control. Our ranking below is editorial and weighs 5 criteria: traffic coverage, identity and authorization, deployment options, maturity, and price transparency. How the 13 best agent gateways rank 1. Kong AI Gateway Kong governs LLM, MCP and A2A traffic from 1 control plane. Version 2.0 moved AI features into first-class Providers, Models, MCP Servers and Agents entities . Best for: teams already running Kong for API management. Watch out: the 2.x architecture needs a Konnect control plane. Arcade notes the MCP OAuth2 plugin is still Tech Preview. 2. Bifrost (Maxim AI) Bifrost is an Apache 2.0 Go gateway covering models, MCP tools and A2A agents in 1 deployment. Maxim reports 10,000+ models across 25+ providers. Its benchmark claims 11 µs mean overhead at 5,000 RPS . Best for: self-hosted, in-VPC or air-gapped teams that want all 3 traffic types. Watch out: SSO, SCIM and token exchange are Enterprise-only. An independent review notes the 11 µs figure excludes HTTP handling and JSON marshalling. 3. Gravitee AI Gateway Gravitee runs an LLM Proxy, MCP Proxy and A2A Proxy on 1 runtime. All 3 share 1 authentication, policy and OpenTelemetry chain. The A2A Proxy supports RFC 8693 token exchange and skill-level authorization. Best for: enterprises that want agent identity modeled alongside existing APIs. Watch out: Maxim lists Agent Management from $2,500 per month. The A2A Proxy needs Enterprise Edition. 4. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway AgentCore Gateway gives agents 1 managed endpoint for tools, models and other agents . It adds semantic tool search, Cedar policies and on-behalf-of token exchange. Pricing starts at $0.005 per 1,000 invocations . Best for: AWS-native teams using IAM, CloudWatch and Bedrock Guardrails. Watch out: AWS-only. A2A is HTTP passthrough, per Maxim . Search calls cost $0.025 per 1,000 , 5x the invoke rate. 5. Arcade.dev Arcade is an actions runtime, not a model router. Per Arcade , it checks the overlap of user and agent permissions on every action. Credentials never reach the LLM. It lists 8,000+ agent-optimized tools. Best for: agents that write to Salesforce, Gmail or Slack on a user’s behalf. Watch out: no model routing, so pair it with an LLM gateway. Pricing is $25 per month plus $0.10 per auth event and $0.01 per tool call. 6. Prisma AIRS AI Gateway (formerly Portkey) Palo Alto Networks completed its Portkey acquisition in May 2026. The gateway reached GA inside Prisma AIRS in July 2026. Palo Alto describes it as a unified LLM, MCP and A2A gateway with 1 enforcement point. It runs in SaaS and hybrid models . Best for: security teams that want runtime inspection on every prompt. Watch out: pricing is not public. Arcade advises verifying delegated auth and audit depth for agent actions. 7. Azure API Management Microsoft’s AI gateway extends API Management to model APIs, MCP servers and A2A agent APIs. It can expose REST APIs as MCP servers and front existing MCP servers. Best for: Microsoft-centric API teams. Watch out: A2A support is preview, JSON-RPC only, and limited to v2 tiers. 8. Google Cloud Agent Gateway Agent Gateway is the network entry and exit point for Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. It assigns each agent a SPIFFE ID and can apply Model Armor to prompts and responses. Maxim lists up to 5,000 governed resources per gateway. Best for: teams building on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Watch out: Maxim reports cross-cloud…

articles.title: Uncommon Thinkers: Andrew Redd’s audacious plan to turn ocean volcanoes into power plants
articles.content: Andrew Redd, CEO and founder of Endurance Energy, with company puppy Maple at the startup’s Seattle HQ. (Endurance Photo) Editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec. 10 at the GeekWire Gala in partnership with Greater Seattle Partners . Andrew Redd ‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup. The dots connect, but the picture they form is anything but ordinary: bold in vision, fast in execution and enormous in potential. Redd has next-level ambition, and he’s directing it at solving one of the world’s biggest and most urgent problems — adding renewable, massively scalable energy that can outcompete fossil fuels and reach the grid quickly enough to make a difference in the race against climate change. Underwater geothermal energy has never been tapped in a significant way, but to Redd, the idea was irresistible. “It checks all of the boxes for our perfect future energy source,” he said. So Redd set out to build it. He founded Endurance Energy on the north shore of Seattle’s Lake Union in January 2025, and this September the team oversaw its fifth deep-sea deployment. At a site 300 miles off the Oregon coast, its prototype system generated more electricity than it consumed. The startup has raised $63 million from investors and has roughly three dozen employees. Nate Bek , a principal at Ascend, praised Redd’s ability to attract “brilliant” talent in pursuit of his goal. The Seattle venture firm is one of the startup’s early backers. “I’ve been deeply inspired by what [Redd]’s building at Endurance and haven’t shut up about it since the day we met,” Bek said. “He somehow makes powering the world from the bottom of the ocean feel inevitable, all while remaining remarkably measured and transparent about the progress.” Keeping the world wide open For Redd, studying engineering and aerospace in college was so clear-cut that it wasn’t a choice at all. Growing up around Boeing, seaplanes, the Museum of Flight and the Pacific Northwest’s rich maritime industry naturally pointed him toward those sectors. He wanted a degree as expansive as his influences. “I didn’t really want to have to choose whether it was going to be boats or space travel or airplanes,” he said. “I just wanted to be able to do anything — keep the world as wide open as possible.” After graduating from Princeton University, Redd worked at Neuralink, an Elon Musk company developing technology that lets the brain communicate directly with computers. A year later, in 2021, he moved to Musk’s rocket company, SpaceX. That was another no-duh decision, as Redd viewed it. “I saw SpaceX as really the place to be, where early-career people are given the most amount of resources and responsibility, and that felt like the fastest way to learn and the most engaging possible scenario to be in,” Redd said. “I wanted to be tossed into something that was a little bit crazy.” Redd joined as SpaceX was starting to build its first orbital Starship rockets. The program brought together passionate young people and experienced SpaceX engineers who served as mentors. Wild ideas were entertained and explored. Everyone was committed to the mission. It was just the experience Redd wanted, and he planned to stick around for seven to 10 years. Then artificial intelligence started booming. Redd on the job. (Endurance Photo) Checking all the boxes In 2024, the build-out of sprawling, energy-hungry data centers for AI was accelerating with no end in sight. At the same time, efforts to electrify transportation, heating and cooling were driving up demand for power. Redd saw these trends sparking a surge in new…

articles.content: TL;DR Google has announced that it will expand Android’s new sideloading and developer verification rules to global markets in January 2027. The company will force all app developers to verify their identities, including apps on the Play Store, Galaxy Store, and several other OEM markets. People who want to sideload unverified apps will need to take plenty of steps, including a 24-hour wait. Google announced developer verification and changes to app sideloading last year. These changes started rolling out in four countries back in September, and the search giant has now announced a date for a global expansion. Google has confirmed a January 2027 global rollout for these new developer rules and sideloading changes:

articles.title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
articles.content: Google announced Android developer verification last year , and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead . It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon. The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure . Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps. In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months." articles.title: The Novilla Bliss is an Amazon best-seller, but is this memory foam mattress worth it? I slept on the budget bed for a month to find out
articles.content: Novilla Bliss Memory Foam 10" Mattress review in brief Insanely popular on Amazon, the Novilla Bliss Memory Foam Mattress is a cheap and cheerful all-foam offering that I freely admit I wasn’t expecting much from. However, there were lots of things about the Novilla Bliss that surprised me in a good way and overall, I was quite impressed by the support considering the mattress’ very reasonable pricing. Meet the tester (Image credit: Jo Plumridge) Name: Jo Plumridge Age bracket: 45-55 Weight bracket: 100-130lbs Predominant sleep position: Combination sleeper who spends slightly more time on her side Sleep issues: Suffers with back pain which can easily be exacerbated by an unsupportive mattress It’s not going to rival the very best mattresses on the market but if you’re on a budget, this should definitely be on your radar. With a queen mattress currently priced at $269.99 in the Black Friday mattress deals , I think this is one of the best budget beds currently on the market. In terms of firmness, I’d suggest that most sleepers will find it at the firmer end of the medium scale. There is sinkage and this is an all-foam mattress, but there’s still some support underneath. I can’t think of any other all-foam mattresses I’ve slept on that are as firm, except for the Nectar Classic Memory Foam . However, I must stress that I’m a lightweight sleeper and my husband, who is lightweight to average weight for a man, found it softer than I did. Still, we both enjoyed it for side sleeping particularly and, as someone who is ultra fussy about lumbar support, I found it more comfortable for back sleeping than I expected. Motion isolation on the Novilla Bliss is exceptional, and I couldn’t feel my husband moving around at all, but edge support is lacking both when you lie or sit on the edge. I didn’t feel as if I’d actually fall off the bed, but there was some definite tilting. Novilla Bliss Memory Foam 10" Mattress Specs Type: Memory Foam Firmness: Medium (lighter sleepers will find it medium firm) Height: 10" Trial period: 100 nights Warranty: 10 years Price: From $179.99 at Novilla The mattress' one big failing, though, is temperature regulation. I sleep cold so this wasn't an issue, but my husband found it stuffy and, while he didn't wake up sweaty, he didn’t find it massively comfortable either. Hot sleepers on a budget might be happier on the Siena 10" Signature mattress , which kept our testers comfortably cool. But value for money is the Novilla Bliss' big selling point and considering its price, I was really impressed overall with the mattress. Read on for my full assessment of the Novilla Bliss Memory Foam mattress so you can decide if it’s worth investing in. Novilla Bliss Memory Foam 10" Mattress review: Price and trial You’ll pay under $300 for a queen, with the mattress currently priced at $269.99 100-night trial, 10-year warranty and free shipping and returns on Novilla’s website 90-day returns, manufacturer warranty and free shipping and returns on Amazon A queen size Novilla Bliss is listed at $269.99 with a 20% discount from $337.99 on the brand’s own website, while Amazon currently has the price at $269.99. This sale price seems to be fairly set, so here are the MSRPs for each size, plus the usual sale price you can expect to pay: Twin: $224.99 (MSRP), $179.99 (Sale / Amazon) Twin XL: $249.99 (MSRP), $199.99 (Sale / Amazon) Full: $299.99 (MSRP), $239.99 (Sale / Amazon) Queen: $337.99 (MSRP), $269.99 (Sale / Amazon) King: $439.99 (MSRP), $351.99 (Sale / Amazon) Of course, November is one of the best times of the year for mattress sales and we’re seeing some Black Friday deals — a twin size Novilla 8" hybrid mattress is down to $90, for example, and on Amazon the queen size 10" Novilla Bliss has dropped below $210 a couple of times in 2026. So, it’s definitely worth keeping an eye on prices but do remember that, at $269.99 for a queen, the Novilla Bliss is already incredibly well priced. Benefits differ very slightly…

articles.title: Anthropic Tops $2 Trillion Market Cap After IPO Debut
articles.content: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest initial public offering in history. Shares opened at $111.50, a 34% premium that briefly pushed the Claude developer's market capitalization above $2 trillion, making it one of the world's most valuable companies. CNBC reports: The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI, now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced a sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. [The Pentagon formally designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk in March following a dispute over military use of its AI models.] Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Amazon’s $18B bet on Anthropic tops $200B, for a moment, in the Claude maker’s historic market debut
articles.content: Anthropic opened at $111.50 a share, valuing the Claude maker at about $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis. (Nasdaq video screenshot) Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut today in a record $81.3 billion initial public offering , with big financial stakes for the Seattle area’s two tech giants. For Amazon, the IPO is a paper windfall. The company started putting money into Anthropic in 2023, about $18 billion in all . At the $83 IPO price, its stake was worth about $161 billion . With Anthropic opening at $111.50 a share, that number was closer to $216 billion. The stock has since dropped below $100, which put Amazon’s stake under $200 billion. Beyond the value of the investment, Anthropic is a major customer for Amazon’s cloud platform. The Claude maker has committed to spend at least $110 billion on Amazon Web Services through 2036. For Microsoft, it’s more complicated. The Redmond company agreed in late 2025 to invest up to $5 billion but hasn’t disclosed the size of its stake. Microsoft is buying $1 billion of Anthropic stock alongside the IPO, one of seven tech companies buying a combined $26 billion. Anthropic has committed to spend at least $47 billion on Microsoft’s Azure cloud through 2033. But Microsoft is also pitching its own AI models against Anthropic’s, and it has been working to replace Anthropic’s models with OpenAI’s in some Copilot features, The Information reported this week. Listing Anthropic’s compute partners on CNBC this morning , co-founder Daniela Amodei named Nvidia, Amazon, Google and Broadcom, but not Microsoft. Whether it was a slip or something more significant, it was an interesting omission. A historic debut: The offering tops SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO in June, and it makes Anthropic the first standalone AI lab to go public, ahead of OpenAI. The five-year-old company was valued at about $1.5 trillion at the $83 IPO price, on a fully diluted basis that counts employee stock and other shares not yet issued. The stock opened at $111.50 , valuing Anthropic at about $2 trillion on the same basis. It has since traded as low as about $95 . Speaking before the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei said Anthropic will slow the training and release of its AI models for as long as it takes to be confident they’re safe, and that going public only strengthens that resolve. “We will not bend to either business nor political pressure,” he said. In an interview with CNBC’s Andrew Ross Sorkin afterward, Amodei called the push and pull between growth and that kind of restraint “one of the central tensions at the heart of the company.” Anthropic is also a public benefit corporation, a structure that legally requires the company to balance shareholders’ interests with the public good. What’s next: Both Seattle-area giants have hedged their bets. Microsoft owns about 24% of OpenAI , and Amazon put $50 billion into OpenAI earlier this year. OpenAI, which confidentially filed for its own IPO in June, is still aiming to go public in 2027. Anthropic’s co-founders and some of its biggest shareholders are barred from selling for up to a year under the IPO’s lock-up rules, and Amazon has said it expects a customary lock-up period. Amazon will update the value of its Anthropic holdings in its fourth-quarter results, much of it through earnings, which means the paper windfall is likely to boost Amazon’s fourth-quarter profit even though it hasn’t sold a share.

articles.title: Your Hulu weekend watch list: Friday (a fantasy adventure's return), Saturday (an Oscar-winning film), Sunday (a reality guilty pleasure)
articles.content: It’s nearly Thanksgiving and, if you’re like us, your brain is already turned off, at least when it comes to anything not turkey- or pie-related. If that’s the case, the last thing you probably want to do is sort through the seemingly endless selection of new movies and TV shows that have dropped on the best streaming services lately. But don’t worry, Tom’s Guide is here to help: We've zeroed in on one top-rated streamer, Hulu , sifted through all of those new arrivals, and narrowed things down to a trio of great titles — one for each night of your weekend. On Friday, dive back into the mythological world of a hit YA fantasy-adventure franchise on Disney+. On Saturday, you can revisit one of the best political dramas in recent memory: an Oscar-winning Brazilian film. And for your indulgently lazy Sunday, here's a little bit of trashy reality TV perfect to soothe your Sunday Scaries: a brand-new California spinoff of a viral TikTok-fueled docuseries. Now all you have to do is remember to pre-order those pumpkin pies. Friday: 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians' season 3 Going into season 3, which adapts Rick Riordan's third book "The Titan's Curse," war has been brewing between the Olympians and the Titans, with demigods dangerously caught in the middle. For his part, young Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell) finds himself surrounded by unlikely allies, including Thalia Grace (Tamara Smart) and the Hunters of Artemis, as he sets out on a perilous journey to rescue Annabeth Chase (Leah Sava Jeffries) from Kronos's evil forces. Not only must Percy free the chained goddess, but he also must confront the Titan's curse and prevent the fall of Olympus—quite a lot for a teenage demigod! The new installments bring in many new Olympian gods, including Hera (Ming-Na Wen), Aphrodite (Kate McKinnon), Demeter (Jennifer Beals), and Apollo (Hubert Smielecki). Stream "Percy Jackson & the Olympians" season 3 on Hulu now Saturday: 'I'm Still Here' This Walter Salles-directed bio-drama made history last year, becoming the first Brazilian production to win Best International Feature Film at the Academy Awards. It also deservedly received awards-body kudos for its stunning lead performance by Fernanda Torres, who earned an Oscar nomination and a Golden Globe win for Best Actress, making her the first Brazilian to win a Globe for acting. Based on Marcelo Rubens Paiva's biographical book, the political drama sees Torres play Eunice Paiva, a mother of five children living in 1970s Rio de Janeiro, who becomes a human rights advocate following the abduction of her husband — the dissident politician Rubens Paiva (Selton Mello) — during the military dictatorship in Brazil. Eunice spends decades searching for the truth of her spouse's disappearance and the regime's involvement in the shattering of her family. Stream "I'm Still Here" on Hulu now Sunday: 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County' season 1 You've met the "Mormon Wives" of Utah's Salt Lake City; now get to know their counterparts in sunny California. Aside from Utah transplant Jen Affleck, we've got a new group of young mothers — including Ashleigh Pease, Jordan McClanahan, McCall DaPron and Madison Bontempo, among others — whose "beliefs are not just their religion; they are their identity." However, like the O.G. series, this spinoff finds those women clashing between wanting to defend their way of life and being open to modernity and change. Per the official series logline: "Scandals and secrets will be revealed, facades will crumble, and families and friendships will change forever on both sides of the battlefield as this group of strong, game-changing influencers comes together to build their answer to #MomTok." articles.title: Perplexity Launches Orchestrator API for Failover and Model Routing
articles.content: Perplexity has launched the Perplexity Orchestrator API , a single endpoint for frontier and open-weight models. It picks a serving provider by availability, capacity and latency , and bills everything through 1 account. Developers get fewer integrations and 1 invoice. What is the Perplexity Orchestrator API? The Perplexity Orchestrator API is a hosted inference gateway that serves many models behind 1 base URL. It covers frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI . It also serves open-weight models such as GLM, Kimi and DeepSeek, hosted by Perplexity or inference partners. It accepts OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages requests. Most teams only change the API key and base URL. The OpenAI base URL is https://api.perplexity.ai/orchestrator/v1 . Anthropic SDK users point at https://api.perplexity.ai/orchestrator , without /v1 . Perplexity runs the same layer internally, across 85+ models and more than a dozen providers. How does provider failover work? Failover keeps the model fixed and swaps the deployment. A Claude request that fails on Anthropic can be served by AWS Bedrock instead. The reliability docs set these rules: Triggers are provider errors, rate limits and timeouts. Each attempt has a time-to-first-token limit and a total-duration limit. The values are not published. Invalid or over-context requests return HTTP 400 and are not retried. If every deployment fails, the API returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After . Requests that fail before producing output are not billed. You cannot pick a deployment yourself. What do the reliability and speed numbers show? Perplexity measured production traffic from October 4 to November 2, 2026. Claude and GPT requests through Perplexity succeeded more often than requests to any single provider measured. Daily success rates also varied less during provider incidents. The post gives no percentage success rates. Speed varied by provider too. For Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic was fastest on 15 of 30 days, AWS Bedrock on 15. Azure’s median output speed for GPT-5.6 Sol was 27% higher than OpenAI’s. Speed-aware routing is still in progress. How does automatic routing with perplexity/auto work? Routing is in preview. You set model to perplexity/auto and pass a routing object. It holds a default_model and 1 to 5 routes , each with a name, description and model. A decision model reads the conversation and route descriptions. It never sees route names or model IDs. If nothing matches, or the decision model fails or times out, the default model answers. So do media inputs. Response headers report the result: x-perplexity-autoroute-outcome , -route and -confidence . The default policy sends traffic to GPT-6.1 Sol, with simple requests going to GPT-6 Luna. Perplexity also lists built-in Lower cost, Balanced and Higher quality profiles, plus an Auto effort preview. Can routing work around refusals? Perplexity tested this on a 63-task subset of Terminal-Bench 4.1 , run in Claude Code. Anthropic documents that Claude Fable 5.2 safeguards can block benign security and life sciences work. Claude Fable 5.2 alone: 38/63 tasks. Fable plus routes to GPT-6.1 Sol: 41/63. Fable plus routes to GPT-6 Astra: 41/63. The routes covered security , biology and after_refusal requests. That is +3 tasks, at a higher estimated cost per task. Perplexity calls it an adjusted comparison; results vary by workload. How is Orchestrator priced? Each request is billed at the answering model’s published per-token rate. Failover to another provider does not change the rate. Perplexity says there is no additional platform fee on top of credits . For example, perplexity/glm-5.3 lists $1.4 input, $4.4 output and $0.26 cache read per 1M tokens . Usage draws from prepaid Perplexity API credits, also purchasable through AWS Marketplace. Access is tiered by cumulative credit purchases : Tier 0: Google, xAI and open-weight models. Tier 1 ($50): OpenAI and most Anthropic models. Tier 2…

articles.title: IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too
articles.content: Coding agents need backups, too, or at least that’s what IDrive is arguing. Backup and storage service IDrive on Thursday announced AI Agents Backup , a feature in its desktop app that finds the data these agents store locally for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex , and Cline and copies it to the user’s IDrive account. By default, agents tend to keep a lot of their state on a developer’s machine, including session transcripts, instruction files, and MCP server configurations. The problem is that most of this sits in hidden folders that developers rarely look at. Thing is, some of this data is actually valuable. A session transcript, after all, is a record of how a developer and an agent got to a fix, and this local data also helps agents like Claude Code and Codex pick up from old sessions to continue a task days later. Then, there are the AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files and things like MCP configurations that involve some setup work that few developers will want to have to redo when something goes awry. Credit: IDrive. As IDrive CEO Raghu Kulkarni notes in the announcement , “Most of that data lives only on the local machine and has been left out of backup plans.” The history and configuration these agents build up, he says, is “a real work product.” Session history is easily lost Some of this data is also easy to lose. By default, Claude Code deletes session transcripts older than 30 days. Users have actually filed a long list of GitHub issues about history that disappeared without warning and Cursor’s forum has plenty of threads from users whose chat history disappeared after an update. What IDrive backs up For Claude, the new backup feature covers Claude Code history from both the terminal and the desktop app, plus settings, instruction files, and local MCP server configurations. It also picks up Cowork scheduled tasks that Team and Enterprise users chose to keep on their own machine. The Cursor backup includes chat history, workspace data, keybindings, extensions, and the Cursor Agent CLI’s sessions. Codex and Cline get similar treatment. It’s worth noting that IDrive skips caches and temporary files. It also doesn’t back up source code and repositories, because the company expects users to protect them with its regular file backup. Any chats that live on a provider’s servers are also out of bounds. When a user wants to restore these files, IDrive puts them back into their original location. One thing to note is that, for Claude, IDrive’s documentation says it replaces whatever is there. Restoring also only works between machines that run the same operating system, which means a Windows setup can’t be restored to a Mac, for example. Open source backup alternatives This idea, of course, isn’t entirely new. Developers can already use a plethora of open source tools to sync and back up their agent’s state. There are tools like bak , which syncs agent configurations, and commercial services like Agent Bak . Agent-archive , meanwhile, ships session transcripts to an S3 or R2 bucket and backup specialist Backblaze’s labs team has published an open source engine for backing up agent state to its B2 storage service. IDrive’s version is built into a consumer backup app and can automatically detect the four agents on its own. It also comes with a restore flow that is meant for moving to a new computer. AI Agents Backup is available now in the IDrive desktop app for all users, the company says. Gemini CLI , GitHub Copilot , and Windsurf aren’t on the supported list. The post IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too appeared first on The New Stack .

articles.title: Anthropic throws open doors at $2T valuation as shares pop 34% in initial trading
articles.content: Welcome to the world of public AI frontier labs: Anthropic is now a publicly-held company with its Thursday IPO, and investors are clamoring for a piece of the pie, for now anyway. That $83 IPO price didn’t last long, with shares rocketing to $111.50 by the time the public could get their hands on them at the end of the initial auction. That means that the company was valued at around $2 trillion as of the public availability of the 980 million shares it put up for sale, a 34 percent increase over the IPO price. At just under six years old, Anthropic’s meteoric rise to that valuation has sent investors into a frenzy despite uncertainties surrounding the company’s future profitability. As we’ve noted, Anthropic is on the hook for nearly $1 trillion in compute obligations that could drag its profitability prospects down if any one of a number of scenarios happens to materialize. Amodei was on hand to address some of those questions with CNBC this morning following the opening of markets on his company’s big day. When asked about the risk Anthropic’s massive compute bills to its bottom line, Amodei admitted the company’s needs are difficult to predict, and that - get this - they try to err on the low side. That’s right: The $900 billion in infrastructure and compute commitments that Anthropic revealed in a recent regulatory filing, which could end up surpassing $1T in short order, might just be an underestimate of what the company will need in coming months and years. Not to worry, though, the Anthropic CEO insisted: It’s worth it. “We’re willing to put into place these very large compute spends because, historically, we’ve seen that it pays off,” Amodei told CNBC’s Ross Sorkin, adding that the returns on the cognitive capabilities of its new models are “so high” as to make all that spending worth it - eventually, one would assume based on his comments, Anthropic is sure to come out on top. But what of the threat of open models that could undermine the constant push at Anthropic and other frontier labs to create the most power-hungry, resource-intensive, and powerful AI? Bah, that’s not a problem either. Frontier model makers like Anthropic, Amodei said, have already proven that they can do the heavy lifting at the bleeding edge, so you can trust it to make reliable models that are cheaper and less capable, too. “Anthropic can compete both at and away from the frontier,” The Anthropic CEO said. Whether that’ll mean long-term success for investors is another thing altogether. Mozilla president Mark Surman doesn’t think valuation translates into long-term success, for one. He told The Register this morning that the one thing he consistently hears from developers is that they want AI they can control, not rent from a frontier lab. As Amodei suggested in his comments, Anthropic is aware that those with less intense AI needs might not choose its models, and that could harm the company. “Pushing AI toward open source matters so much right now,” Surman said in an email. “Mozilla’s own research this year found that open source models account for a third of all tokens, while the gap with the best closed models is down to about 3.3 per cent.” In other words, keep an eye on that Anthropic stock - it might be hot now, but reality could still catch up to the company with the biggest-ever IPO. “The market is already moving,” Surman said. “No valuation changes that.” ®

articles.title: Gamers Skip Work to Play GTA VI After 13-Year Wait
articles.content: After a 13-year wait, Rockstar games' Grand Theft Auto VI has officially (and finally) launched today to near-universal acclaim, earning a 99/100 score on Metacritic and generating an estimated $1.84 billion from 19 million copies sold. The highly anticipated release has prompted gamers to take time off work, attracted nearly 2 million concurrent Twitch viewers, and sparked celebrations around the world. "Video game critics have lauded it, describing it as a 'masterpiece' and 'the single most impressive video game' they've ever played," reports NBC News. An expert told Reuters that there could be a "work blackout across the board." Another expert suggested that $1 billion in U.S. productivity could be lost as people take time off to play the game, which is estimated to take about 50 hours to complete. Here's a roundup of GTA VI reviews: IGN (10/10) calls it "the single most impressive video game I have ever played." GameSpot (10/10) praises its extraordinary attention to detail, calling it a culmination of Rockstar's open-world achievements. Push Square (10/10) describes it as Rockstar's deepest and most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2, though it notes the 30fps cap and occasional pacing issues. Eurogamer (5/5) praises its ambitious world and the emotional depth of Jason and Lucia's relationship. Digital Foundry highlights its groundbreaking visual realism, ray tracing, and simulation detail, while acknowledging compromises from the 30fps target. Bloomberg calls it an all-time classic, praising the unpredictable interactions and remarkable freedom of exploration. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: NAND prices tipped to fall as Chinese cloud giants cut SSD orders
articles.content: NAND flash prices could start falling next year as Chinese cloud operators cut enterprise SSD orders, helping push the market toward oversupply. Taiwan-based market intelligence firm TrendForce says Chinese cloud service providers are grappling with GPU shortages, high inventories, and fierce competition over AI token pricing. As a result, they have reduced their total enterprise SSD orders for 2027 by a substantial amount. Although TrendForce doesn't specify any figures, it says the cutbacks in China are large enough to outweigh the additional demand coming from US-based cloud operators. But don't get too excited: TrendForce forecasts overall NAND flash contract prices falling by 0-5 percent quarter on quarter in early 2027, with all product categories entering a downturn from the second quarter. Falling orders are only half the story. Manufacturers are also increasing output, while weaker consumer electronics sales could further depress demand. Strong demand for high-performance storage in the US continues to drive manufacturers to expand capacity and upgrade to newer process technologies. At the same time, the rising adoption of quad-level cell (QLC) technology and increasing number of layers in the NAND chips will further boost bit output, TrendForce observes. Some suppliers may go slower on their expansion plans in response to sluggish consumer demand, but the firm still expects global NAND flash output, measured in storage capacity, to grow by 25 to 30 percent in 2027. US restrictions on access to advanced AI chips could put Chinese cloud operators under further pressure. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has introduced new restrictions on sales of GPUs, and on remote access to them via the cloud. The new restrictions " set everyone back in China ," as The Register reported. TrendForce adds the caveat to its forecast that its market outlook depends on factors such as the pace of inventory reduction among Chinese CSPs, further changes to the restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether device makers continue reducing storage capacities in 2028. Sadly, cheaper NAND wouldn't resolve the separate squeeze on DRAM supplies. The situation, caused by memory makers opting to produce high-margin products for the AI market rather than mainstream chips, has already increased prices of PCs in Europe by double-digit percentages, leading to a fall in shipments as buyers balk at the cost. ®

articles.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
articles.content: Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nyhamna_footage_take5_30s.mp4 AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation. AI agents built on Falkor’s agentic engine understand dense technical documentation, spatial relationships and real-world physics. Engineers can create and test plans in simulation before traveling on site, reducing costly delays and mistakes. They can also inspect equipment and check clearances in a shared view. Read Falkor’s article and watch the livestream f or a closer look at how the company builds these tools and checks the agents’ work. Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation With SimReady Assets Getting a robot model into a scene is only the start. Developers also need to assemble its components, add controls and check whether it can complete a task. NVIDIA developers Dillon Bailey and Rishabh Chadha used 3D assets from the SimReady Central library to build a pick-and-place simulation of a robot moving a can using the NVIDIA Isaac Sim framework. They directed an agent equipped with GPT-6 Sol and Isaac Sim skills to assemble the scene and generate pick-and-place controls. Testing the assembled scene shows how the assets work together, from joint movement and contact behavior to the gripper’s ability to hold, move and release the can. With that baseline in place, developers can adjust object positions and motion paths and repeat the tests to evaluate how each change affects the task. Follow the walkthrough to assemble and test a pick-and-place simulation in Isaac Sim, with sample agent prompts and checks for robot movement and grasp behavior. Build a Voice-Controlled VR Simulation With SimReady Assets Bringing 3D assets into virtual reality (VR) requires more than rendering a scene. Objects need to respond to controllers and behave as expected when grabbed, moved or released. NVIDIA Omniverse community developer Michael Wagner took on this challenge. He directed GPT-6 Astra to use Blender software to model a study environment from two reference images, balancing visual quality with efficient performance in VR. He then used Claude Code to build an application that lets users find SimReady Central assets by voice and interact with them in an immersive VR scene. The Claude Code agent worked for about eight hours, and Wagner built the application over a weekend using an NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada workstation and a Meta Quest 3 VR headset. The application ran on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries : ovstage shared the OpenUSD scene, ovrtx rendered it, ovxr enabled VR and ovphysx ran physics. articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals a strategy to undercut its AI rivals
articles.content: Welcome to AI Decoded , Fast Company ‘s weekly newsletter that breaks down the most important news in the world of AI. I’m Mark Sullivan, a senior writer at Fast Company , covering emerging tech, AI, and tech policy. Sign up to receive this newsletter every week via email here . And if you have comments on this issue and/or ideas for future ones, drop me a line at sullivan@fastcompany.com, and follow me on X @thesullivan . ‘Compute multipliers’ and ‘Anthropic Direct’ may be the IPO’s secret sauce As frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google converge in capabilities, the companies selling them may end up competing for enterprise business less on model quality and more on the cost of the computing power needed to run them. In its IPO filing and investor roadshow video, Anthropic, which debuted on the Nasdaq on Thursday, suggested it may be preparing for that future with something called “compute multipliers” and a compute-sourcing model it calls Anthropic Direct. In its S-1, filed publicly in October, Anthropic defines compute multipliers as “algorithmic and methodological” improvements in the way it trains and operates models, effectively increasing the computing power it can get from a given amount of capacity. And these multipliers are “stackable.” In its roadshow video , Anthropic says it measures “total effective compute,” which is its physical computing capacity multiplied by the multipliers it has discovered or expects to discover in the future. Its example: If a model takes 100 units of compute to train, a 4x multiplier lets Anthropic train the same model with 25 units, or use all 100 units to train a model that would previously have required 400. The company also says the multipliers “stack,” with each new discovery building on previous ones, and that it expects Claude will eventually be able to discover multipliers on its own. According to the filing, the gains apply to models used to serve customers as well as to model training. Anthropic says its researchers “have delivered meaningful compute multipliers for inference,” reducing the computing power needed to deliver a given level of model performance. The company says this “allows us to provide greater value for customers.” Anthropic has already been cutting prices. It says price reductions tied to new model versions, along with contractual discounts, reduced revenue growth by about $600 million between the second and third quarters of 2026. It says Opus 5.5, launched in September, delivered “a lower cost per task” than earlier models. If Anthropic can get more usable compute out of each chip than its rivals can, it may be able to undercut other AI labs on price. It may also be able to undercut cloud providers that sell AI services built on their own models. If compute multipliers let Anthropic do more with its physical computing power, Anthropic Direct could give the company greater control over where that power comes from. Right now, Anthropic buys almost all its computing power from cloud providers, including competitors like SpaceX, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, and CoreWeave. The company says it has already committed to buying roughly $900.9 billion in compute from these providers over the coming years and decades. Those expenses also include short-term cloud compute purchases, mainly to cover peak usage periods, which come at a premium. The S-1 says Anthropic is reducing its reliance on expensive cloud providers by developing its own data centers and leasing the chips that go inside them. Its first Anthropic Direct facility came online this year. The company says a “significant portion” of its planned compute spending will go toward building more Anthropic Direct capacity. Based on an analysis of contract values in the S-1 filing, PitchBook estimates that Direct data centers will supply about 1% of Anthropic’s available compute capacity this year, 48% in 2030, and 60% in 2035. articles.title: As widespread tech outages pile up, AI tools are in the spotlight again
articles.content: Inaccessible email inboxes . Banking delays . And a communications meltdown that grounded airplanes for hours, followed by waves of other travel disruptions. In an increasingly interconnected world, some fear such disruptions could be the new normal. Over the past week alone, problems that appeared to emerge from routine updates, security patches or other malfunctions surfaced at Microsoft , JP Morgan Chase and Apple , and even the U.S. government’s Federal Aviation Administration and National Security Agency. The Trump administration said there was “zero” indication the latest outages are linked, or caused by bad actors like cybercriminals . The era of artificial intelligence has also raised the stakes for internet security overall. As AI tools uncover new vulnerabilities, many other companies and institutions are racing to patch them before they can be targeted by hackers, a cat-and-mouse game that can lead to a different set of glitches. Social media platforms have been abuzz with a mixture of annoyance, confusion, conspiracy theories and jokes about the string of outages. “To see several disruptions this close together, I think to a lot of people it’s made them realize how many parts of their lives they’ve handed over to these systems that we still, at this point, don’t fully understand,” Jake Smith, a content creator who regularly posts videos about politics on platforms like Instagram and YouTube, said in an interview. “I think it gives people a sense of helplessness to see all of it happening concurrently in a way.” What’s gone offline recently Outages and technology errors have piled up across sectors. Late last week, a global Microsoft outage disrupted email and other workplace tools, plunging business and everyday services into disarray worldwide. Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Microsoft cited, in part, a failure during a recent upgrade to its servers, spanning from what the company later determined was a “latent defect” in a network fix it had begun deploying over the summer. For air travel, a separate malfunction in the FAA’s network led to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years on Friday. The stop lasted for more than four hours, and carriers cancelled and delayed swaths of flights as they worked to recover. Just days later, United Airlines saw its own system outage — forcing it to delay departing flights on Monday. Online banking troubles also piled up on Monday. JPMorgan Chase said a software bug affected its internal hardware systems — causing transactional delays for its customers and others sending money to related accounts, sending jitters throughout the financial system before the problem was resolved. And on Tuesday, Apple, Marriott and the NSA joined the growing list. Apple Music, the App Store and AppleCare services were temporarily disrupted after the company said an internal update caused outages. And Marriott said a technical issue also caused problems for sign-ins on its website and app. Meanwhile, the NSA said an internal network it uses to communicate classified information was also offline Tuesday “during scheduled routine maintenance.” The government — as well as Microsoft, United, JPMorgan Chase, Apple and Marriott — have again maintained there’s no evidence of these disruptions being linked or related to a cyberattack . Microsoft also noted that its outage did not span from “AI / agents,” although it didn’t immediately specify the goal of the network fix it first deployed over the summer. Microsoft did not respond to an Associated Press request for further details, and the other companies did not provide additional comments Wednesday about their disruptions when contacted by the AP via email. AI has helped identify vulnerabilities, but also adds to risks AI has nonetheless come into the spotlight as experts…

articles.title: A “headless Slack”: Vercel’s new message board lets Claude Code and Codex agents work together
articles.content: For AI agents to work together effectively, they need a way to communicate and divvy up tasks — much as humans already do through a swath of digital collaboration tools. Vercel is tackling this with Board , an experimental shared message board through which agents can claim tasks, exchange findings and track progress across different tools and environments, while allowing developers to follow and intervene in the work. In a blog post published on Wednesday, Vercel says it developed Board for its own engineering operations, first using it to coordinate security agents investigating vulnerabilities and submitting fixes. It then rebuilt v0 ’s software factory around Board, which Vercel says now “merges over 50% of PRs.” “It packages what we’ve learned about coordinating work across agent fleets.” “It packages what we’ve learned about coordinating work across agent fleets and builds towards a future where multiple teams of humans and agents orchestrate swarms, software factories, and other agentic workflows,” the company writes. The coordination conundrum OpenAI demonstrated the importance of multi-agent communication in September when it announced that its agents had solved the Navier–Stokes problem, a longstanding mathematical challenge concerning the behavior of fluids. The company said some 10,000 agents operated concurrently in the group that produced the result, exchanging information as they worked. “In the process of resolving the Navier–Stokes problem, the agents sent 2.7 million messages and used approximately 130 billion output tokens,” the company wrote. The need to manage multiple agents in parallel is becoming increasingly apparent in software development. Just last week, Google and Cursor introduced competing approaches to coordinating coding agents, with Google focusing on agents working on behalf of a single developer and Cursor enabling agents belonging to different teammates to communicate. Then on Tuesday, Replit introduced Missions , bringing multiple agents together to tackle larger development projects. Elsewhere, companies are also turning to existing collaboration platforms to bring humans and AI agents together. Devin Bots , which Cognition launched on Tuesday , uses Slack to connect agents with their human teammates. In an X post published on Thursday, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says more than 226,000 custom agents have been deployed to Slack from across the major agent-building platforms. Notably, he says that he hadn’t anticipated this use of Slack when Salesforce acquired it back in 2021 , acknowledging that companies are now using the platform as “trusted agent infrastructure.” Vercel itself added its Agent to Slack code channels in August, allowing teammates to follow its work, give instructions and review proposed changes. With Board, Vercel provides channels and threaded discussions where agents can pick up assignments, exchange findings, monitor dependencies and record completed work. It also maintains a history of activity, allowing developers to follow what their agents have been doing. Crucially, Board is designed to accommodate agents built on different technologies. Vercel explicitly lists Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra and LangChain, as tools that can work together through Board. “This is an important building block for software factories, self-optimizing systems, and scientific research.” In an X post published on Wednesday, Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch described the technology as a “message board infrastructure primitive.” Or, a “headless Slack” for agents. “This is an important building block for software factories, self-optimizing systems, and scientific research, where the human prompting is just the seed of the system, and millions of agents can operate in a decentralized fashion,” Rauch writes, adding that Board is…

articles.title: Build Tool-Calling Parsers in Rust with AI Agents
articles.content: A tool call can arrive in pieces, an argument can be cut short, or model-specific markup can leak into the answer. A frontend parser turns that output, received... A tool call can arrive in pieces, an argument can be cut short, or model-specific markup can leak into the answer. A frontend parser turns that output, received as token IDs or decoded text, into visible text, reasoning, and tool calls an application can use.
