articles.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
articles.content: By Richard Anton Panics and pile-ons are a familiar pattern in the public markets, with a herd mentality wiping value from companies in an instant. Trading can swiftly become a barometer of emotions, rather than a well-informed gauge of value. We have seen this play out with AI’s impact on software companies and the supposed end of the Software as a Service business model. The doom-laden talk of the SaaSpocalypse was noise, with little signal, and most traders were initially unable to distinguish between a company that will thrive in the AI age and one that will be decimated by it. The SaaSpocalypse didn’t reveal the end of software. It revealed the limits of public markets in judging its value. This pattern erodes trust in the public markets. For companies, being publicly owned may no longer be appealing, and founders considering an exit may not view an initial public offering as the ultimate goal. How the markets got it wrong Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx. The markets have struggled to keep up with the tech advances of the AI era and judge their impact on incumbent companies. Sometimes they underreacted and ignored these developments, and other times they overreacted and panicked. When OpenAI launched ChatGPT to the public in November 2022, Alphabet stock was punished even though later Google emerged as a clear winner with generative AI. And with SaaS, the markets were slow to respond to the advent of generative and agentic AI through to the end of 2025. The market capitalization of enterprise software companies continued to rise through this period, until January 2026 when all hell broke loose. The launch of Claude Cowork triggered a panic, especially when additional plug-ins were announced later that month that targeted specific workflows for enterprise support functions such as HR and legal. From there, valuations went into a tailspin, with traders treating software companies indiscriminately. Over two days, an estimated $285 billion of market capitalization was wiped from software, data analytics and financial tech companies, and by April the benchmark cloud software index — the BVP Nasdaq Emerging Cloud Index — had dropped by 31% since the start of the year. As an investor in software over many decades, I have seen this pattern many times before. AI does not mean the end of software companies. Rather, AI has driven a shift in how software is built, where user growth will come from — primarily agents rather than humans — and in the sources of defensible competitive advantage. This was always going to benefit some companies, like those deeply embedded into their customers’ core business processes, and harm others. The recovery has been uneven and markets still get it wrong There were predictions of the death of SaaS, but this is the hype cycle pattern that always plays out when new technology emerges: a surge of excitement, then a correction, then productivity. In the short term, the markets overestimated the harm AI would inflict on the software sector as a whole. That is now being corrected as the markets start to realize which companies benefit from AI and which are threatened by it. At the end of October, the cloud software index was up by 26% since the start of the year and by a massive 83% since its nadir in April. At my firm, Oxx , we never believed in the SaaSpocalypse, and the markets have recovered from this turmoil. The recovery is bifurcated with some sub sectors, like cybersecurity and data and analytics, faring well while others, like workflow management, have fallen back. In cybersecurity, a great example is CrowdStrike , whose share price dropped by 27% in early 2026 but was up 114% between the start of the year and the end of October. The problem with public markets is part of a bigger trend The knee-jerk reactions to the latest developments with AI, however, are not just temporary market sentiment. They are part of a broader shift that has occurred since the late 1990s and…

articles.title: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
articles.content: Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering. The feat, whose details are pending publication, was carried out in Sydney after a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano connected a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste. In an interview, Pulitano, a transplant surgeon at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital and a professor at the University of Sydney, likened the life support system to “an artificial body.” Its official name is the Extended Organ Perfusion System. “Our group is the only one in the world to have maintained a human liver under fully normothermic, physiological conditions for seven weeks,” he says. Normothermic means body temperature, or about 37 °C. The previous record for keeping an internal organ alive outside the body was set in Switzerland several years ago. That organ—also a liver—lasted around two weeks. Most organs destined for transplant survive only a few hours in special ice buckets and need to be raced to their destination. Over the last decade, however, surgeons have been switching to perfusion systems, which pump warm or cold fluids into an organ. This can double the time it can be held before it must be transplanted. Pulitano says the key to breaking the record was to automate the systems used to keep the organ thriving. During a meeting in Switzerland earlier this year, the Sydney team described perfusing 55 human livers, one after the other. Some were connected to a system that needed to be adjusted manually, but for those placed on the automated system—which produced the seven-week survivor—the average survival time tripled, to about four weeks. Perfusion has already enabled doctors to restart hearts from dead people and keep them beating outside the body. Paulo Martins, a transplant doctor at the University of Oklahoma, says about half the kidneys he transplants are now perfused, even though the process can add $100,000 to the cost of a transplant. While the research awaits formal publication, the eventual goal is what Pulitano and colleagues call “time-unlimited liver preservation.” Scientists have already discovered possible medical benefits to keeping organs on life support longer than usual. One, they say, is that perfused organs apparently start to repair themselves and become stronger after a day or so. That’s what led a Swiss team, in 2022, to transplant a damaged liver that had been kept on perfusion for three days —the longest time any internal organ had remained outside the body before a successful transplant, says Waldemar Hoffmann, the CEO and cofounder of Apersys, a startup formed to commercialize the technology. Pulitano says his own startup, Aeternum Life Technologies, will be helping with a planned trial in Sydney to transplant low-quality livers kept on perfusion for four days. What’s less clear, says Hoffmann, is whether any transplant surgeon would ever want, or need, to use an organ kept alive for nearly two months. He says people in the field believe Pulitano’s record is real, but they don’t know how healthy the organ was at the end or even what so much extra time is likely to achieve. “The key question is what the purpose for a seven-week perfusion would be,” he says. Yet that’s where things could start to get interesting, says Martins , the Oklahoma surgeon. Long-term life support could enable far-out concepts like artificial wombs, new types of organ manufacturing, and the chance to experiment directly on human organs outside the body for extended periods. For his part, Pulitano says long-term machine perfusion could help grow new organs. In living donations, surgeons commonly take half of a person’s liver to give someone else. articles.author: Radhika Rajkumar
articles.fingerprint: employers half interview like look reject resumes use yet
articles.titleFa: ۹۰٪ کارفرمایان، رزومه‌هایی که شبیه به هوش مصنوعی هستند را رد می‌کنند – اما نیمی از آن‌ها برای مصاحبه از هوش مصنوعی استفاده می‌کنند
articles.summaryFa: در بازار کار امروز، کارجویان تا چه حد می‌توانند در برابر ابزارهای استخدام مبتنی بر هوش مصنوعی مقاومت کنند؟ با اینکه ۹۰٪ از کارفرمایان رزومه‌هایی که شبیه به تولیدات هوش مصنوعی هستند را رد می‌کنند، نیمی از آن‌ها همچنان از هوش مصنوعی برای برگزاری مصاحبه‌ها استفاده می‌کنند.
articles.summaryEn: In today's job market, how much choice do applicants really have regarding compliance with AI hiring tools? While 90% of employers reject resumes that resemble AI-generated content, half of them still use AI for conducting interviews.
insightsFa: بسیاری از کارفرمایان به دنبال سبک‌های سنتی‌تر رزومه هستند.
استفاده از هوش مصنوعی در مصاحبه‌ها در حال افزایش است.
کارجویان با چالش‌های جدیدی در پذیرش این ابزارها مواجهند.
تقابل بین سنت و نوآوری در فرآیند استخدام واضح است.
کارجویان باید استراتژی‌های خود را متناسب با این تغییرات به‌روزرسانی کنند.
articles.whyItMattersFa: این خبر نشان‌دهنده تضاد میان نیازهای کارفرمایان و چگونگی سازگاری کارجویان با فناوری‌های جدید است. در حالی که هوش مصنوعی در استخدام در حال گسترش است، چالش‌هایی همچون اولویت‌بندی بر روی تنوع و خلاقیت در رزومه‌ها وجود دارد.

articles.title: The Governance Gap in Open-Weight AI and What to Do About It
articles.content: Lower costs, data privacy, and greater control are driving open-weight AI adoption, but many organizations are not addressing the risks that come with it. The post The Governance Gap in Open-Weight AI and What to Do About It appeared first on SecurityWeek .
articles.author: Etay Maor
articles.fingerprint: about gap governance open weight
articles.titleFa: فاصله در حکمرانی هوش مصنوعی با وزن باز و راهکارهای آن
articles.summaryFa: استفاده از هوش مصنوعی با وزن باز به دلیل هزینه‌های پایین‌تر، حفظ حریم خصوصی داده‌ها و کنترل بیشتر در حال افزایش است، اما بسیاری از سازمان‌ها به خطرات ناشی از آن توجهی نمی‌کنند. این مقاله به بررسی چالش‌های حکمرانی در استفاده از هوش مصنوعی با وزن باز و راهکارهای آن می‌پردازد.
articles.summaryEn: The adoption of open-weight AI is increasing due to lower costs, data privacy, and greater control. However, many organizations are not addressing the risks associated with it. This article discusses the governance challenges of open-weight AI and potential solutions.
insightsFa: هوش مصنوعی با وزن باز به کاهش هزینه‌ها و حفظ حریم خصوصی داده‌ها کمک می‌کند.
بسیاری از سازمان‌ها خطرات مربوط به استفاده از هوش مصنوعی با وزن باز را نادیده می‌گیرند.
این مقاله به شفاف‌سازی چالش‌های حکمرانی در این حوزه می‌پردازد.
باید راهکارهایی برای مدیریت خطرات هوش مصنوعی با وزن باز پیشنهاد شود.
پیشرفت در حکمرانی می‌تواند به بهبود اعتماد و پذیرش این تکنولوژی کمک کند.
articles.whyItMattersFa: این خبر اهمیت دارد زیرا استفاده از هوش مصنوعی با وزن باز در حال افزایش است و عدم توجه به خطرات آن می‌تواند مشکلات جدی برای سازمان‌ها ایجاد کند. همچنین، راهکارهای مناسب می‌توانند منجر به بهبود امنیت و کارایی این تکنولوژی شوند.

articles.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
articles.content: One of the early targets of PHP2Shell exploitation was the firewall. On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting the two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws let anyone execute code on the web server without authentication. The disclosure itself went a little wrong.
articles.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
articles.fingerprint: application everything firewall including web your
articles.titleFa: همه چیز یک وب‌اپلیکیشن است، حتی دیوار آتش‌تان
articles.summaryFa: در تاریخ ۲۸ اکتبر، شرکت Palo Alto Networks تأیید کرد که مهاجمان با بهره‌برداری از دو آسیب‌پذیری PHP، به‌ویژه CVE-2026-109618 و CVE-2026-109619، به رابط‌های مدیریت PAN-OS که به اینترنت متصل بودند، حمله می‌کنند. این دو آسیب‌پذیری اجازه می‌دهند تا هر کسی بدون نیاز به احراز هویت، روی سرور وب کد اجرا کند.
articles.summaryEn: On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws allow anyone to execute code on the web server without authentication.
insightsFa: آسیب‌پذیری‌های PHP با CVE-2026-109618 و CVE-2026-109619 شناسایی شده‌اند.
این نقص‌ها به مهاجمان اجازه می‌دهند بدون احراز هویت کدهای مخرب روی سرور اجرا کنند.
حملات به دیوار آتش یکی از اهداف کلیدی مهاجمان قرار گرفته است.
اطلاعات منتشر شده به صورت ناقص به اطلاع عموم رسید.
توجه به امنیت در وب‌اپلیکیشن‌ها و دیوارهای آتش از اهمیت بالایی برخوردار است.
articles.whyItMattersFa: این خبر اهمیت دارد زیرا نشان‌دهنده نحوه آسیب‌پذیری دیوارهای آتش در برابر حملات سایبری و نیاز به تقویت امنیت در زیرساخت‌های اینترنتی است.
